title.zh: 卷五十一 列傳第四十一 梁宗室上
title.en: Volume 51 Biographies 41: The Liang Imperial Family 1
title.raw: 卷五十一 列傳第四十一 梁宗室上 Volume 51 Biographies 41: The Liang Imperial Family 1

sentences.zh: 列傳第四十一梁宗室上

translations.literal: Biographies 41: The Liang Imperial Family, Part 1
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 41 — The Liang Imperial Family, Part One

sentences.zh: 吳平侯景長沙宣武王懿永陽昭王敷衡陽宣王暢桂陽簡王融臨川靖惠王宏

translations.literal: Marquis Jing of Wu Ping, Prince Xuanwu of Changsha Yi, Prince Zhao of Yongyang Fu, Prince Xuan of Hengyang Chang, Prince Jian of Guiyang Rong, Prince Jinghui of Linchuan Hong
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Jing of Wu Ping; Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi; Prince Zhao of Yongyang, Fu; Prince Xuan of Hengyang, Chang; Prince Jian of Guiyang, Rong; and Prince Jinghui of Linchuan, Hong

sentences.zh: 景，崇之子也。

translations.literal: Jing was the son of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was a son of Chong.

sentences.zh: 八歲，隨父在郡，居喪以毀聞。

translations.literal: At eight years of age he accompanied his father in the commandery; his mourning conduct was famed for its severity.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight, he went with his father to the commandery, and his mourning conduct became known for its severity.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，才辯有識斷。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning; he was talented in debate and possessed discernment.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he loved learning and was gifted in debate, with sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為永寧令，政為百城最。

translations.literal: In Qi service he was magistrate of Yongning; his administration ranked first among the hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he served as magistrate of Yongning, and his governance was rated the best in the realm.

sentences.zh: 永嘉太守范述曾居郡，號稱廉平，雅服景為政，乃牓郡門曰：「諸縣有疑滯者，可就永寧令決。」

translations.literal: Fan Shuzeng of Yongjia, who governed the commandery and was styled incorrupt and fair, greatly admired Jing's administration and posted at the commandery gate: "If any county has doubtful or stalled cases, they may be settled by the magistrate of Yongning."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shuzeng, governor of Yongjia, was known as incorrupt and even-handed and greatly admired Jing's governance. He posted a notice on the commandery gate: "Counties with doubtful or stalled cases may bring them to the magistrate of Yongning for decision."

sentences.zh: 以疾去官。

translations.literal: He left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 永嘉人胡仲宣等千人詣闕表請景為郡，不許。

translations.literal: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others went to the capital to petition that Jing be made governor of the commandery; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhongxuan of Yongjia and a thousand others petitioned at court for Jing to be made commandery governor, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，以長沙宣武王懿勳，除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, on account of the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, he was appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year 2, on the merit of Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, he was appointed colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 是冬懿遇害，景亦逃難。

translations.literal: That winter Yi met with violence and died; Jing also fled into hardship.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yi was killed; Jing fled as well.

sentences.zh: 武帝起兵，以景行南兗州事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu raised his army, he had Jing act as governor of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took up arms, he put Jing in charge of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 時天下未定，沔北傖楚，各據塢壁。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was not yet settled; north of the Han, Cang and Chu peoples each held fortified stockades.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still unsettled; north of the Han, tribal groups each held fortified stockades.

sentences.zh: 景示以威信，渠帥相率面縛請罪，旬日境內皆平。

translations.literal: Jing displayed authority and good faith; chieftains came in succession, bound themselves, and begged pardon, and within ten days the whole territory was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jing won them over with authority and trust; chieftains came forward in succession, bound themselves, and begged pardon, and within ten days the whole region was at peace.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，封吳平縣侯，南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wu Ping County, made Governor of Southern Yan Province, and given the additional title of Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Jing was enfeoffed as marquis of Wu Ping county, made governor of Southern Yan Province, and given overall command.

sentences.zh: 詔景母毛氏為國太夫人，禮如王國太妃，假金章紫綬。

translations.literal: An edict made Jing's mother, Lady Mao, Grand Lady of the State, with rites like those of a princely grand consort, and granted her a golden seal on a purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Jing's mother, Lady Mao, grand lady of the state with rites like a princely grand consort, and granted her a golden seal on a purple cord.

sentences.zh: 景居州清恪，有威裁，明解吏職，文案無壅，下不敢欺，吏人畏敬如神。

translations.literal: Jing governed the province with purity and strictness, possessed authority and judgment, understood official duties clearly, and had no backlog in documents; subordinates did not dare deceive him, and officials and commoners revered him as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As governor he was scrupulous and stern, understood official business thoroughly, and kept paperwork moving; subordinates did not dare cheat him, and officials and commoners revered him almost as a deity.

sentences.zh: 會年荒，計口振恤，又為饘粥于路以賦之，死者給棺具，人甚賴焉。

translations.literal: When famine struck, he counted mouths and gave relief; he also set out gruel by the roads to distribute, and provided coffins for the dead; the people relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When famine came, he counted households and gave relief, set out gruel by the roads, and provided coffins for the dead; the people depended on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 天監七年，為左驍騎將軍，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianjian he became General of Valiant Cavalry on the Left and concurrently General Who Commands the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 7 he became general of valiant cavalry on the left and concurrently general who commands the army.

sentences.zh: 領軍管天下兵要，宋孝建以來，制局用事，與領軍分權，典事以上皆得呈奏，領軍垂拱而已。

translations.literal: The post of Commander of the Army controlled the realm's military essentials; since Xiaojian of Song, the Bureau of Regulations had held power, sharing authority with the commander; officials of director rank and above could all submit memorials directly, and the commander merely held his hands in his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of the army controlled the realm's military essentials; since Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the Bureau of Regulations had shared power with the post, and directors and above could submit memorials directly while the commander merely nodded along.

sentences.zh: 及景在職峻切，官曹肅然，制局監皆近幸，頗不堪命，以是不得久留中。

translations.literal: When Jing held the post he was stern and exacting; the offices were solemn; the supervisors of the Bureau of Regulations were all imperial favorites and could hardly bear his commands, and for this reason he could not long remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was stern and exacting in office; the bureaus fell silent. The bureau supervisors were imperial favorites and could hardly bear his rule, so he could not remain long at court.

sentences.zh: 尋出為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Colonel Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Governor of Yong Province, with the additional title of Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as colonel who pacifies the barbarians and governor of Yong Province, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 八年，魏荊州刺史元志攻潺溝，驅迫群蠻，群蠻悉度漢水來降。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yuan Zhi, Wei Governor of Jing Province, attacked Chan'gou and drove the various Man tribes; all the tribes crossed the Han to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Yuan Zhi, Wei governor of Jing Province, attacked Chan'gou and drove the tribal peoples; they all crossed the Han to surrender.

sentences.zh: 議者以為蠻累為邊患，可因此除之。

translations.literal: Counselors held that the Man had long been a border affliction and could be eliminated on this occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers argued that the tribes had long troubled the frontier and could be wiped out now.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「窮來歸我，誅之不祥；

translations.literal: Jing said, "Having come to the end of their strength to submit to us, to execute them would be inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "They have come to us in desperation; to kill them would be ill-omened;

sentences.zh: 且魏人來侵，每為矛楯，若悉誅蠻，則魏軍無礙，非長策也。」

translations.literal: moreover when Wei men come to invade, they have always served as spear and shield; if we kill all the Man, the Wei army will meet no obstacle—this is no long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: and when Wei invades, they have always served as our shield. If we slaughter them all, the Wei army will meet no barrier—that is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 乃開樊城受降，因命司馬朱思遠、甯蠻長史曹義宗、中兵參軍孟惠雋擊志於潺溝，大破之。

translations.literal: He then opened Fancheng to receive their surrender and ordered his Chief of Staff Zhu Siyuan, Chief Clerk Cao Yizong, and Army Controller Meng Huijun to strike Zhi at Chan'gou and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He opened Fancheng to receive them, then sent Chief of Staff Zhu Siyuan, chief clerk Cao Yizong, and army controller Meng Huijun against Zhi at Chan'gou and routed him.

sentences.zh: 景初到州，省除參迎羽儀器服，不得煩擾吏人。

translations.literal: When Jing first arrived in the province, he abolished the welcoming ceremonies, guard insignia, and ceremonial dress, and would not trouble officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing first took the province, he cut welcoming ceremonies, guard insignia, and formal dress, and would not burden officials or commoners.

sentences.zh: 修葺城壘，申警邊備，理辭訟，勸農桑。

translations.literal: He repaired walls and ramparts, strengthened frontier alerts, settled lawsuits, and encouraged agriculture and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired walls and ramparts, tightened frontier defenses, heard lawsuits, and encouraged farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 郡縣皆改節自勵，州內清靜，抄盜絕跡。

translations.literal: Commanderies and counties all reformed their conduct and encouraged themselves; within the province there was quiet, and banditry vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies and counties reformed themselves; the province grew quiet and banditry disappeared.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復為領軍將軍，直殿省，知十州損益事，月加祿五萬。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again became General Who Commands the Army, attended the Hall Directorate, oversaw matters of gain and loss in ten provinces, and received an additional salary of fifty thousand per month.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he again became general who commands the army, attended the hall directorate, oversaw fiscal matters in ten provinces, and received fifty thousand extra in monthly salary.

sentences.zh: 景為人雅有風力，長於辭令。

translations.literal: Jing as a man possessed refined force of character and excelled in rhetoric.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had natural dignity and excelled in eloquence.

sentences.zh: 其在朝廷，為眾所瞻仰。

translations.literal: In court he was looked up to by all.
translations.idiomatic: At court everyone looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 于武帝雖屬為從弟，而禮寄甚隆，軍國大事皆與議決。

translations.literal: Although to Emperor Wu he was a cousin, the courtesy and trust shown him were very lofty; major military and state affairs were all decided with his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Though only a cousin to Emperor Wu, he was treated with exceptional honor; major military and state affairs were all decided with his counsel.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 及太尉、揚州刺史臨川王宏坐法免，詔景以安右將軍監揚州，置佐史，即宅為府。

translations.literal: When the Grand Commandant and Governor of Yang Province, Prince Hong of Linchuan, was removed for an offense, an edict had Jing, as General of Secure Right, supervise Yang Province, appoint aides and clerks, and make his residence the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant and Yang governor Prince Hong of Linchuan was dismissed for an offense, an edict put Jing, as general of secure right, in charge of Yang Province, with staff appointed and his own residence as headquarters.

sentences.zh: 景越親居揚州，固讓至於涕泣，帝弗許。

translations.literal: Jing, though junior in kinship, held Yang Province; he firmly declined until he wept, but the Emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Though junior in kinship, Jing was put over Yang Province; he declined until he wept, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 在州尤稱明斷，符教嚴整。

translations.literal: In the province he was especially famed for clarity and decisiveness; his orders and instructions were strict and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he was especially famed for clear judgment; his orders were strict and prompt.

sentences.zh: 有田舍老姥訴得符，還至縣，縣吏未即發，姥語曰：「蕭監州符如火，汝手何敢留之！」

translations.literal: An old village woman who had won a writ returned to her county; the county clerk did not issue it at once. The old woman said, "Supervisor Xiao's writ is like fire—how dare your hand keep it!"
translations.idiomatic: An old village woman who had won a writ returned to her county, but the clerk did not issue it at once. She said, "Supervisor Xiao's writ is like fire—how dare you hold it back!"

sentences.zh: 其為人所畏敬如此。

translations.literal: Such was the awe and respect he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the awe he inspired.

sentences.zh: 遷都督、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as commander-in-chief and governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 將發，帝幸建興苑餞別，為之流涕。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the Emperor visited Jianxing Park to give a farewell banquet and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, the emperor came to Jianxing Park to bid him farewell and wept.

sentences.zh: 在州復有能名。

translations.literal: In the province he again won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he again won renown for competence.

sentences.zh: 齊安、竟陵郡接魏界，多盜賊，景移書告示，魏即焚塢戍保境，不復侵略。

translations.literal: Qi'an and Jingling commanderies bordered Wei and had many bandits; Jing sent letters of notice, and Wei at once burned its stockades and garrisons to guard the border and no longer invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Qi'an and Jingling bordered Wei and were plagued by bandits; Jing sent notices, and Wei burned its stockades and garrisons to guard the border and stopped raiding.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumously he was given the title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Cord, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous name Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumously he was made grand master with golden seal and purple cord, equal in honor to the three excellencies, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子勱。

translations.literal: His son was Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xun.

sentences.zh: 勱字文約，弱不好弄，喜慍不形於色。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Wenyue, in youth did not care for play; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, styled Wenyue, as a boy disliked play; joy and anger never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 位太子洗馬，母憂去職，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: He held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent; when his mother died he left office and could scarcely bear the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as groom of the heir apparent; when his mother died he left office and nearly could not survive his grief.

sentences.zh: 每一思至，必徒步之墓。

translations.literal: Whenever the thought came upon him, he would walk on foot to the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever grief seized him, he walked on foot to the tomb.

sentences.zh: 或遇風雨，僕臥中路，坐地號慟，起而復前，家人不能禁。

translations.literal: Sometimes he met wind and rain; servants would fall by the road, he would sit on the ground wailing, rise and go on again—his family could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: In wind and rain servants collapsed on the road; he would sit wailing on the ground, rise, and go on—his family could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 景特所鍾愛，曰：「吾百年後，其無此子乎。」

translations.literal: Jing especially cherished him and said, "A hundred years hence, will I not lack this son?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing especially loved him and said, "When I am gone, will I not lack this son?"

sentences.zh: 使左右節哭。

translations.literal: He had those about him moderate his weeping.
translations.idiomatic: He had attendants moderate his weeping.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子中舍人。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Palace Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made palace attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 景薨於郢鎮，或以路遠，秘其凶問，以疾漸為辭。

translations.literal: When Jing died at the Ying garrison, some, because the road was long, concealed the news of death and spoke gradually of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing died at Ying, some concealed the death because of the distance and spoke only gradually of illness.

sentences.zh: 勱乃奔波，屆于江夏，不進水漿者七日。

translations.literal: Xun then rushed about and arrived at Jiangxia; for seven days he took no water or broth.
translations.idiomatic: Xun rushed off and reached Jiangxia; for seven days he took no food or drink.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓所，親友隔絕。

translations.literal: He built a hut at the tomb and cut himself off from kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut at the tomb and cut himself off from kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 會叔父曇下詔獄，勱乃率昆弟群從同詣大理，雖門生故吏，莫能識之。

translations.literal: When his uncle Tan was sent to the imperial prison, Xun led brothers and cousins together to the Court of Justice; even students and former subordinates could not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Tan was imprisoned, Xun led brothers and cousins to the court of justice; even his students and former subordinates could not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 後襲封吳平侯，對揚王人，悲慟嗚咽，傍人亦為隕涕。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Wu Ping; facing the Yang king's envoy, he wept and sobbed, and those beside him also shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the marquisate of Wu Ping; facing the Yang king's envoy, he wept until those beside him wept too.

sentences.zh: 除淮南太守，以善政稱。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Huainan and was famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Huainan and was famed for good governance.

sentences.zh: 遷宣城內史，郡多猛獸，常為人患，及勱在任，獸暴為息。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Interior Secretary of Xuancheng; the commandery had many fierce beasts that were often a menace to people, but while Xun held office the beasts' ravages ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He was made interior secretary of Xuancheng, where fierce beasts had long troubled the people; under Xun their attacks ceased.

sentences.zh: 又遷豫章內史，道不拾遺，男女異路。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as Interior Secretary of Yuzhang; things lost on the road were not picked up, and men and women walked on separate paths.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made interior secretary of Yuzhang, where no one picked up lost goods on the road and men and women walked on separate paths.

sentences.zh: 徙廣州刺史，去郡之日，吏人悲泣，數百里中，舟乘填塞，各齎酒肴以送勱。

translations.literal: He was moved to Governor of Guang Province; on the day he left the commandery, officials and commoners wept; for several hundred li boats and carriages filled the roads, each bringing wine and food to send Xun off.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Guang Province; on the day he left, officials and commoners wept, and for hundreds of li boats and carts clogged the roads as people brought wine and food to see him off.

sentences.zh: 勱人為納受，隨以錢帛與之。

translations.literal: Xun had his men accept the gifts and then gave them money and silk in return.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had his men accept the gifts and then gave money and silk in return.

sentences.zh: 至新淦縣岓山村，有一老姥以盤擎鰍魚，自送舟側奉上之，童兒數十人入水扳舟，或歌或泣。

translations.literal: At Qishan village in Xingan county, an old woman bore loach on a tray, came to the side of the boat herself, and presented them; several dozen children entered the water to hold the boat, some singing, some weeping.
translations.idiomatic: At Qishan village in Xingan county an old woman brought loach on a tray to the boat and presented them; dozens of children waded in to hold the boat, singing or weeping.

sentences.zh: 廣州邊海，舊饒，外國舶至，多為刺史所侵，每年舶至不過三數。

translations.literal: Guang Province bordered the sea and was formerly rich; when foreign ships arrived, they were often encroached upon by the governor, and each year no more than three or so ships came.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Province lay on the sea and was once prosperous; foreign ships were often preyed on by governors, and only two or three arrived each year.

sentences.zh: 及勱至，纖豪不犯，歲十餘至。

translations.literal: When Xun arrived, not even the smallest was violated, and more than ten came each year.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xun not even the smallest sum was taken, and more than ten ships came each year.

sentences.zh: 俚人不賓，多為海暴，勱征討所獲生口寶物，軍賞之外，悉送還台。

translations.literal: The Li people did not submit and often raided by sea; what Xun gained in campaigns—captives and valuables—beyond military rewards, he sent all back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Li did not submit and often raided by sea; captives and booty from Xun's campaigns, beyond military rewards, all went back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 前後刺史皆營私蓄，方物之貢，少登天府。

translations.literal: Governors before and after all amassed private stores; tribute goods rarely reached the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier governors had all amassed private wealth; local tribute rarely reached the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 自勱在州，歲中數獻，軍國所須，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: From the time Xun was in the province, several offerings were made each year; what the army and state required came in succession without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xun several shipments went up each year; military and state needs were met without interruption.

sentences.zh: 武帝歎曰：「朝廷便是更有廣州。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "The court has gained another Guang Province."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu sighed and said, "The court has gained another Guang Province."

sentences.zh: 有詔以本號還朝，而西江俚帥陳文徹出寇高要，又詔勱重申蕃任。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to court with his former title, but the Li chieftain Chen Wenche of the West River raided Gaoyao, and another edict had Xun resume his post on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him at his former rank, but Li chieftain Chen Wenche of the West River raided Gaoyao, and another edict sent Xun back to the frontier post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，文徹降附。

translations.literal: Before long Wenche surrendered and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenche surrendered.

sentences.zh: 勱以南江危險，宜立重鎮，乃表台于高涼郡立州。

translations.literal: Xun held that the southern river region was perilous and a major garrison should be established; he memorialized the capital to establish a province at Gaoliang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xun argued that the southern river region was dangerous and needed a major garrison; he memorialized to establish a province at Gaoliang commandery.

sentences.zh: 敕仍以為高州，以西江督護孫固為刺史。

translations.literal: An edict still made it Gaozhou and appointed Sun Gu, Protector of the West River, as governor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established Gaozhou and appointed Sun Gu, protector of the West River, as governor.

sentences.zh: 徵為太子左衛率。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left commandant of the heir apparent's guard.

sentences.zh: 勱性率儉，而器度寬裕，左右嘗將羹至胸前翻之，顏色不異，徐呼更衣。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was frank and frugal, yet his bearing was generous; once when an attendant was bringing soup it spilled on his chest, yet his expression did not change and he calmly called for a change of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was plain and frugal but magnanimous; once when an attendant spilled soup on his chest, his expression never changed and he calmly asked for fresh clothes.

sentences.zh: 聚書至三萬卷，披翫不倦，尤好東觀漢記，略皆誦憶。

translations.literal: He collected books to thirty thousand scrolls and read them without weariness; he especially loved the Han Records of the Eastern Observatory and could recite them from memory in the main.
translations.idiomatic: He collected thirty thousand scrolls and read without tiring; he especially loved the Han Records of the Eastern Observatory and could recite most of it from memory.

sentences.zh: 劉顯執卷策勱，酬應如流，乃至卷次行數亦不差失。

translations.literal: Liu Xian would hold a scroll and quiz Xun; he answered like flowing water, even to scroll, section, and line number without error.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian would quiz him from a scroll; Xun answered fluently, even to scroll, section, and line without error.

sentences.zh: 少交結，唯與河東裴子野、范陽張纘善。

translations.literal: He made few associations; only with Pei Ziye of Hedong and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang was he close.
translations.idiomatic: He kept few associates; only Pei Ziye of Hedong and Zhang Zuan of Fanyang were close friends.

sentences.zh: 卒於道，贈侍中，諡曰光侯。

translations.literal: He died on the road; posthumously he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the posthumous name Marquis Radiant.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road; posthumously he was made attendant-in-ordinary, with the posthumous name Marquis Radiant.

sentences.zh: 勱弟勸。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother was Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother was Quan.

sentences.zh: 勸字文肅，少以清靜自立，封西鄉侯，位南康內史，太舟卿。

translations.literal: Quan, styled Wensu, in youth established himself through purity and quiet; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xixiang, held the post of Interior Secretary of Nankang, and was Minister of the Great Boats.
translations.idiomatic: Quan, styled Wensu, won repute in youth for purity and restraint; he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xixiang and served as interior secretary of Nankang and minister of the great boats.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，與南康王會理謀誅侯景，事發遇害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao, with Prince Huili of Nankang he plotted to kill Hou Jing; when the affair was exposed he met with violence and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Dabao year 1 he plotted with Prince Huili of Nankang to kill Hou Jing; when the plot was exposed he was killed.

sentences.zh: 勸弟勉。

translations.literal: Quan's younger brother was Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's younger brother was Mian.

sentences.zh: 勉字文祗，封東鄉侯，位太子洗馬，及勸同見害。

translations.literal: Mian, styled Wenzhi, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxiang, held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent, and met the same fate as Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, styled Wenzhi, was enfeoffed as marquis of Dongxiang, served as groom of the heir apparent, and was killed along with Quan.

sentences.zh: 勉弟勃位定州刺史，封曲江鄉侯。

translations.literal: Mian's younger brother Bo held the post of Governor of Ding Province and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang Township.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's younger brother Bo was governor of Ding Province and marquis of Qujiang township.

sentences.zh: 大寶初，廣州刺史元景仲將謀應侯景，西江督護陳霸先攻景仲，迎勃為刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Dabao, Yuan Jingzhong, Governor of Guang Province, was about to plot in support of Hou Jing; Chen Baxian, Protector of the West River, attacked Jingzhong and welcomed Bo as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dabao, Guang governor Yuan Jingzhong was about to side with Hou Jing; Chen Baxian, protector of the West River, attacked Jingzhong and installed Bo as governor.

sentences.zh: 時湘東王繹在荊州，雖承制授職，力不能制，遂從之。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yi of Xiangdong was in Jing Province; though he issued commissions under his provisional regime, he lacked the power to control matters and therefore followed along.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Xiangdong was then in Jing Province; though he issued commissions under his provisional regime, he could not control events and went along.

sentences.zh: 勃乃鎮嶺南，為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Bo then held the southern ranges and became Governor of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bo then held the southern ranges as governor of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 後江表定，以王琳代為廣州，以勃為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: Later when the lands south of the Yang were settled, Wang Lin replaced him in Guang Province and Bo was made Governor of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the south was pacified, Wang Lin replaced him in Guang and Bo was made governor of Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 魏克江陵，勃復據廣州。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, Bo again seized Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling, Bo again seized Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 敬帝承制，加司徒。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, under his provisional regime, added the title of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing, under his provisional regime, made him minister of education.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，為太尉，尋進為太保。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era he became Grand Commandant and soon advanced to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era he became grand commandant and soon grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 及陳武禪代之際，舉兵不從，尋敗，遇害。

translations.literal: When Chen Wu took the throne by abdication, he raised troops and did not submit; soon he was defeated and met with violence.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wu seized the throne, Bo raised troops and refused to submit; he was soon defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 昌字子建，景弟也。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Zijian, was Jing's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, styled Zijian, was Jing's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 位衡州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the post of Governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 性好酒，在州每醉，徑出入人家，或獨詣草野，刑戮頗無期度，醉時所殺，醒或求焉，亦無悔也。

translations.literal: His nature loved wine; in the province whenever drunk he would go straight in and out of people's houses, or go alone into meadows and wilds; punishments and executions were quite without regular measure—those killed while drunk, when sober he might seek them out, yet he felt no regret.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine; drunk in the province he would walk into people's houses or wander alone in the wilds. Executions followed no rule—men killed while he was drunk he might ask about when sober, yet he never regretted it.

sentences.zh: 累遷兼宗正卿，屢為有司所劾。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to concurrent Minister of the Imperial Clan and was often impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to concurrent minister of the imperial clan and was often impeached.

sentences.zh: 久留都，忽忽不樂，遂縱酒虛悸。

translations.literal: Long remaining in the capital, he was restless and unhappy, and so gave himself to drink in empty alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Long in the capital, he grew restless and unhappy and drowned his fears in drink.

sentences.zh: 在石頭東齋，引刀自刺而卒。

translations.literal: In the eastern studio at Shitou he drew a knife and stabbed himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern studio at Shitou he drew a knife and stabbed himself to death.

sentences.zh: 弟昂。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Ang.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother named Ang.

sentences.zh: 昂字子明，位輕車將軍，監南兗州。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Ziming, held the post of General of Light Chariots and supervised Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, styled Ziming, served as general of light chariots and supervised Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 初，兄景再為兗州，德惠在人，及昂來代，時人方之馮氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, his elder brother Jing had twice held Yan Province; his virtue and kindness remained among the people. When Ang came to replace him, people of the time likened them to the Feng clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his elder brother Jing had governed Yan Province twice, and his kindness still lived in people's hearts. When Ang succeeded him, contemporaries compared the succession to that of the Feng family.

sentences.zh: 徵為琅邪、彭城二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was summoned and made Administrator of the two commanderies of Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as governor of Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 時有女子年二十許，散髮黃衣，在武窟山石室中，無所修行，唯不甚食。

translations.literal: At the time there was a woman of about twenty years, with loose hair and yellow robes, in a stone chamber on Mount Wuku; she practiced no cultivation, only ate very little.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a woman of about twenty, hair loose and clad in yellow, lived in a stone cell on Mount Wuku. She undertook no religious discipline and scarcely ate.

sentences.zh: 或出人間，時飲少酒，鵝卵一兩枚，人呼為聖姑。

translations.literal: Sometimes she came out among people; she would occasionally drink a little wine and one or two goose eggs; people called her the Holy Maiden.
translations.idiomatic: She sometimes appeared among people, drinking a little wine and one or two goose eggs. They called her the Holy Maiden.

sentences.zh: 就求子往往有效，造者充滿山谷。

translations.literal: Those who went to seek sons often had success; visitors filled the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Women who came seeking sons often bore children, and pilgrims packed the valleys.

sentences.zh: 昂呼問無所對，以為祅惑，鞭之二十。

translations.literal: Ang called and questioned her; she answered nothing. He took it for demonic delusion and gave her twenty lashes with the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Ang summoned and questioned her, but she would not answer. Thinking her an occult fraud, he had her flogged twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 創即差，失所在。

translations.literal: Her wounds at once healed; she vanished, her whereabouts unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Her wounds healed immediately, and she disappeared without a trace.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年，為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong, he became General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongdatong (529), he was made general of the guards.

sentences.zh: 久之，封湘陰侯，出為江州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangyin and sent out as Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiangyin and appointed governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰恭侯。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 昂弟昱字子真，少而狂狷，不拘禮度，異服危冠，交遊冗雜。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Yu, styled Zizhen, was from youth wild and obstinate, unrestrained in ritual propriety, wearing strange dress and towering caps, with miscellaneous and vulgar companions.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's younger brother Yu, styled Zizhen, was wild and headstrong from youth, heedless of propriety, fond of outlandish dress and tall caps, and kept company with a riffraff crowd.

sentences.zh: 尤善屠牛，業以為常。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at slaughtering cattle and made it his regular trade.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at butchering cattle and made a living at it.

sentences.zh: 於宅內酤酒。

translations.literal: He sold wine within his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He ran a wine shop in his own house.

sentences.zh: 好騎射。

translations.literal: He loved riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He loved riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 歷位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed through offices to become Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to gentleman attendant at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 每求試邊州，武帝以其輕脫無威望，抑而不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sought assignment to a border province for trial service; Emperor Wu, because he was frivolous and lacked authority, held him back and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked for a border post, but Emperor Wu, judging him reckless and without gravitas, refused each time.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎，上表請自解，帝手詔責之，坐免官。

translations.literal: He was moved to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; he submitted a memorial requesting his own dismissal. The Emperor personally wrote an edict reproving him, and he was dismissed from office on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to attendant at the yellow gate, he memorialized asking to resign. The emperor answered with a personal edict of rebuke, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 因此杜門絕朝覲。

translations.literal: Because of this he shut his gates and ceased attending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he shut his doors and ceased appearing at court.

sentences.zh: 普通五年，坐於宅內鑄錢，為有司所奏，下廷尉，得免死，徙臨海郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Putong, on account of casting coin within his residence, he was impeached by the relevant offices, sent down to the Court of Justice, was spared death, and exiled to Linhai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Putong (524), he was impeached for minting coins at home, tried by the court of justice, spared execution, and exiled to Linhai.

sentences.zh: 行至上虞，有敕追還，令受菩薩戒。

translations.literal: When his journey reached Shangyu, an imperial order recalled him and directed that he receive the bodhisattva precepts.
translations.idiomatic: On the road at Shangyu he was recalled by imperial order and instructed to take the bodhisattva precepts.

sentences.zh: 既至，恂恂盡禮，改意蹈道，持戒又精潔。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was respectful and fulfilled all ritual; he changed his intent and walked the Way, keeping the precepts with refined purity.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was humble and scrupulous in ritual, turned his heart to the Buddhist path, and kept the precepts with exceptional purity.

sentences.zh: 帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 以為晉陵太守，下車勵名跡，除煩苛，明法憲，嚴於奸吏，旬日之間，郡中大安。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Jinling; on taking office he encouraged reputation and merit, removed vexations and severity, clarified laws and statutes, and was stern toward corrupt officials—in the space of ten days the commandery was greatly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Made governor of Jinling, he fostered good reputation from the day he arrived, swept away harsh petty rule, clarified the laws, and cracked down on corrupt clerks. Within ten days the commandery was at peace.

sentences.zh: 俄而暴卒，百姓行號巷哭，市里為之喧沸，設祭奠於郡庭者四百餘人。

translations.literal: Soon he died suddenly; common people wailed in the lanes as they walked, and the marketplaces clamored for him. More than four hundred set up offerings in the commandery courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly soon after. People wailed in the streets, the markets rang with lament, and more than four hundred held memorial rites in the commandery hall.

sentences.zh: 田舍有婦女夏氏年百餘歲，扶曾孫出郡，悲泣不自勝。

translations.literal: In a hamlet was a woman of the Xia clan over a hundred years old; she supported her great-grandson and came out to the commandery, weeping beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: A peasant woman of the Xia clan, more than a hundred years old, led her great-grandson to the commandery seat and wept beyond consolation.

sentences.zh: 其惠化所感如此。

translations.literal: Thus were the people moved by his benevolent influence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the power of his benevolent rule over the people.

sentences.zh: 百姓相率為立廟建碑，以紀其德，又詣都表求贈諡。

translations.literal: The common people in succession built him a shrine and erected a stele to record his virtue, and also went to the capital to submit a memorial requesting a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The people raised a shrine and stele in his honor and sent a delegation to the capital to petition for a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 詔贈湘州刺史，諡曰恭子。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the post of Governor of Xiang Province; his posthumous title was Zi Gong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him governor of Xiang Province posthumously and gave him the title Gongzi, "The Reverent."

sentences.zh: 文帝十男：張惶後生長沙宣武王懿、永陽昭王敷、武帝、衡陽宣王暢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen had ten sons: by Queen Zhang Houang—Prince Xuanwu of Changsha Yi, Prince Zhao of Yongyang Fu, the future Emperor Wu, and Prince Xuan of Hengyang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had ten sons. Queen Zhang bore Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi; Prince Zhao of Yongyang, Fu; the future Emperor Wu; and Prince Xuan of Hengyang, Chang.

sentences.zh: 李太妃生桂陽簡王融。

translations.literal: Lady Li, imperial consort, bore Prince Jian of Guiyang, Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li bore Prince Jian of Guiyang, Rong.

sentences.zh: 融為東昏所害，敷、暢齊建武中卒，武帝踐阼，並追封郡王。

translations.literal: Rong was killed by Emperor Donghun; Fu and Chang died in the Jianwu era of Qi. When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, all were posthumously enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was killed by Emperor Donghun; Fu and Chang died under the Qi in the Jianwu era. When Emperor Wu took the throne, all three were posthumously enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 陳太妃生臨川靖惠王宏、南平元襄王偉。

translations.literal: Lady Chen, imperial consort, bore Prince Jinghui of Linchuan Hong and Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen bore Prince Jinghui of Linchuan, Hong, and Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping, Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳太妃生安成康王秀、始興忠武王憺。

translations.literal: Lady Wu, imperial consort, bore Prince Kang of Ancheng Xiu and Prince Zhongwu of Shixing Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wu bore Prince Kang of Ancheng, Xiu, and Prince Zhongwu of Shixing, Dan.

sentences.zh: 費太妃生鄱陽忠烈王恢。

translations.literal: Lady Fei, imperial consort, bore Prince Zhonglie of Poyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Fei bore Prince Zhonglie of Poyang, Hui.

sentences.zh: 長沙宣武王懿字元達，文帝長子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, styled Yuanda, was Emperor Wen's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuanwu of Changsha, Yi, styled Yuanda, was Emperor Wen's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 少有令譽，解褐齊安南邵陵王行參軍，襲爵臨湘縣侯。

translations.literal: In youth he had fine repute; he doffed the commoner's cloth as a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling under the An'nan command of Qi, and inherited the rank of Marquis of Linxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Famous in youth, he entered service as a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling under the An'nan command in Qi and inherited the marquisate of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 歷位晉陵太守，以善政稱。

translations.literal: He passed through offices to Administrator of Jinling and was famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Jinling and was known for sound administration.

sentences.zh: 永明末，為梁、南秦二州刺史，加督。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongming era he was made Governor of the two provinces Liang and South Qin, with the additional title of Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming he became governor of Liang and South Qin, with supervisory authority.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏軍入漢中，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: That year Wei troops entered Hanzhong and then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei forces entered Hanzhong and laid siege to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 懿隨機拒擊，乃解圍遁去。

translations.literal: Yi responded according to opportunity and resisted; then the siege was raised and they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Yi struck back as circumstances allowed until the besiegers broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又遣氐帥楊元秀攻取魏曆城等六戍。

translations.literal: He also sent the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu to attack and seize the six Wei garrisons including Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the Di leader Yang Yuanxiu to capture six Wei garrisons, including Licheng.

sentences.zh: 魏人震懼，邊境遂寧。

translations.literal: The Wei people were shaken with fear, and the frontier was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the border was secured.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，裴叔業據豫州反，懿以豫州刺史領曆陽、南譙二郡太守討之，叔業懼，遂降魏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye held Yuzhou and rebelled. Yi as Governor of Yuzhou and concurrent Administrator of the two commanderies Liyang and Nanqiao campaigned against him; Shuye was afraid and then surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan (500), Pei Shuye rebelled while holding Yuzhou. Yi, as governor of Yuzhou and concurrent governor of Liyang and Nanqiao, marched against him. Shuye, in fear, defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 武帝時在雍州，遣典簽趙景悅說懿興晉陽之甲，誅君側之罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was then in Yong Province; he sent chief clerk Zhao Jingyue to persuade Yi to raise the army of Jinyang and punish the crime at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was then in Yong Province and sent his chief clerk Zhao Jingyue to urge Yi to raise troops as at Jinyang and punish the evil advisors at court.

sentences.zh: 懿不答。

translations.literal: Yi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 既而平西將軍崔慧景入寇，奉江夏王寶玄圍台城，齊室大亂，馳信召懿。

translations.literal: Before long the General Who Pacifies the West, Cui Huijing, invaded, supporting the Prince of Jiangxia, Bao Xuan, in besieging the capital fortifications; the Qi house fell into great disorder, and messengers were hurriedly sent to summon Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward General Who Pacifies the West Cui Huijing invaded, enthroned Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia, and besieged the imperial city. The Qi court fell into chaos, and urgent summons went to Yi.

sentences.zh: 懿時方食，投箸而起，率銳卒三千人入援。

translations.literal: Yi was then at his meal; he cast down his chopsticks and rose, leading three thousand sharp troops to enter as reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was at table when the call came. He dropped his chopsticks, rose at once, and led three thousand picked troops to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 武帝馳遣虞安福下都說懿曰：「誅賊之後，則有不賞之功，當明君賢主，尚或難立；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu hurriedly sent Yu Anfu down to the capital to say to Yi: "After the rebels are executed, you will have achievements beyond reward. Even with a wise and enlightened ruler, it may still be hard to establish yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu urgently sent Yu Anfu to the capital to tell Yi: "Once the rebels are dead, your merit will be beyond any reward. Even with a wise sovereign, you may still find yourself impossible to accommodate;

sentences.zh: 況於亂朝，何以自免。

translations.literal: how much the more in a disorderly court—how would you save yourself?
translations.idiomatic: how much more so in a court in chaos—how will you protect yourself?

sentences.zh: 若賊滅之後，仍勒兵入宮，行伊、霍故事，此萬世一時。

translations.literal: If after the rebels are destroyed you still marshal troops into the palace and act the precedent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, this is the chance of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: If, once the rebels fall, you march into the palace and follow the precedent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, that is the chance of a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 若不欲爾，便放表還曆陽，托以外拒為事，則威振內外，誰敢不從。

translations.literal: If you do not wish thus, then put forth a memorial and return to Liyang, taking external defense as your pretext—then your authority will shake within and without, and who would dare not follow?
translations.idiomatic: If you prefer otherwise, submit a memorial and return to Liyang on the pretext of guarding the frontier. Your authority will awe court and camp alike, and who will refuse to obey?

sentences.zh: 一朝放兵，受其厚爵，高而無人，必生後悔。」

translations.literal: In one morning you release your troops and accept their thick enfeoffments—lofty yet without support, you will surely come to regret."
translations.idiomatic: But if you lay down your arms for a rich enfeoffment, you will stand too high with no one to support you—and regret will come.

sentences.zh: 長史徐曜甫亦苦勸，並不從。

translations.literal: The Chief Administrator Xu Yaofu also urgently urged him, but he would not follow either.
translations.idiomatic: The chief administrator Xu Yaofu pressed him hard as well, but Yi would not listen to anyone.

sentences.zh: 慧景遣其子覺來拒，懿擊大破之，乘勝而進，慧景眾潰，追斬之。

translations.literal: Huijing sent his son Jue to resist; Yi attacked and smashed him greatly, pressed the victory forward, Huijing's troops collapsed, and pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing sent his son Jue to block him. Yi routed them utterly, pressed the pursuit, and when Huijing's army collapsed he hunted down and slew him.

sentences.zh: 授尚書令、都督征討水陸諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister Director of Affairs and Commander-in-Chief for the punitive campaign over all military affairs on land and water.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister director of affairs and supreme commander of land and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 懿名望功業素重，武帝本所崇敬。

translations.literal: Yi's fame, repute, and achievements had always been weighty; Emperor Wu had long revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's fame and achievements had always been great, and Emperor Wu had long revered him.

sentences.zh: 帝以天監元年四月丙寅即位，是日即見褒崇。

translations.literal: The Emperor took the throne on the bingyin day of the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian; that same day Yi was seen and honored.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the fourth month of the first Tianjian year (502), the day Emperor Wu took the throne, Yi was honored in person.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，乃始贈第二兄敷、第四弟暢、第五弟融。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day, only then were the second elder brother Fu, the fourth younger brother Chang, and the fifth younger brother Rong posthumously granted titles.
translations.idiomatic: Only on the wuchen day did he posthumously enfeoff his second brother Fu, fourth brother Chang, and fifth brother Rong.

sentences.zh: 至五月，有司方奏追皇考皇妣尊號，遷神主於太廟。

translations.literal: Reaching the fifth month, the relevant offices only then memorialized to extend posthumous honorific titles to his imperial father and mother and move their spirit tablets to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the fifth month did the authorities memorialize to bestow posthumous titles on his father and mother and move their spirit tablets to the grand ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 帝不親奉，命臨川王宏侍從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not attend in person; he ordered Prince Hong of Linchuan to attend and serve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not attend in person and had Prince Hong of Linchuan perform the rites.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝臨軒，遣兼太尉、散騎常侍王份奉策上太祖文皇帝、獻皇后及德皇后尊號。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor faced the hall; he sent Acting Grand Commandant and Regular Attendant Wang Fen bearing the patent to present the honorific titles upon Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen, Empress Xian, and Empress De.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor took the throne hall and sent acting grand commandant Wang Fen to present patents raising his father to Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen and honoring the empresses Xian and De.

sentences.zh: 既先卑後尊，又臨軒命策，識者頗致譏議焉。

translations.literal: Since he had first honored the humble and afterward the exalted, and also commanded the patent from the throne hall, those with discernment largely raised critical remarks.
translations.idiomatic: Having honored his brothers before his parents and commanding the patent from the throne hall drew considerable criticism from observers.

sentences.zh: 懿子業字靜曠，幼而明敏，仕齊為太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yi's son Ye, styled Jingkuang, was intelligent and keen from youth; in Qi service he was a Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's son Ye, styled Jingkuang, was clever as a boy and served the Qi as an attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宣武之難，與二弟藻、象俱逃匿于王嚴秀家。

translations.literal: At the crisis of Prince Xuanwu, together with his two younger brothers Zao and Xiang he all hid in the house of Wang Yanxiu.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis of Prince Xuanwu, he fled with his brothers Zao and Xiang to the home of Wang Yanxiu.

sentences.zh: 東昏知之，收嚴秀付建康獄，考掠備極，乃以鉗拔手爪，至死不言，竟以免禍。

translations.literal: Emperor Donghun learned of it; Yanxiu was arrested and handed to the Jiankang prison; torment was applied to the utmost. They used pincers to pull out his fingernails, yet to death he did not speak, and in the end the disaster was avoided.
translations.idiomatic: When Donghun learned of it he seized Yanxiu and threw him into the Jiankang jail, torturing him to the limit and tearing out his fingernails with pincers. Yanxiu never spoke, and the princes escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，襲封長沙王，歷位秘書監，侍中，都督南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he inherited enfeoffment as Prince of Changsha; he passed through offices to Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant, and Commander-in-Chief as Governor of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Tianjian year (503) he succeeded to the princedom of Changsha, then served as director of the secretariat, palace attendant, and regional commander as governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 運私邸米，僦人作甓以砌城，武帝善之。

translations.literal: He transported grain from his private residence and hired men to make bricks to build the wall; Emperor Wu approved.
translations.idiomatic: He shipped rice from his own stores and hired men to make bricks for the city walls. Emperor Wu praised him.

sentences.zh: 徙湘州，尤著善政。

translations.literal: He was moved to Xiang Province and especially distinguished himself in good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Xiang Province, he distinguished himself for excellent governance.

sentences.zh: 零陵舊有二猛獸為暴，無故相枕而死。

translations.literal: Lingling had long had two fierce beasts that were violent; without cause they lay pillow upon the other and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lingling had long been terrorized by two fierce beasts that suddenly died together, each atop the other, for no apparent reason.

sentences.zh: 郡人唐睿見猛獸傍一人曰：「刺史德感神明，所以兩猛獸自斃。」

translations.literal: A man of the commandery, Tang Rui, saw beside the beasts a man who said: "The governor's virtue moved the divine; therefore the two fierce beasts died of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Tang Rui saw a figure beside the beasts who said, "The governor's virtue has moved heaven, and so the two beasts perished of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 言訖不見，眾並異之。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he was not seen; all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking, the figure vanished. All who heard it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 業性敦篤，所在留惠。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was honest and sincere; wherever he went he left kindness behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was by nature earnest and sincere, and wherever he served he left his kindness behind.

sentences.zh: 普通四年，為侍中、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong he was Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Putong (523) he became palace attendant and grand master of splendor with the purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰元王。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Prince Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Yuan.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His literary collection circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子孝儼嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孝儼字希莊，射策甲科，除秘書郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: Xiaoyian, styled Xizhuang, placed in Grade A in the archery-and-plan examination; he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyian, styled Xizhuang, took first rank in the civil examination and was made secretary gentleman and attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 從幸華林園，於坐獻相風烏、華光殿、景陽山等頌，其文甚美，帝深賞異之。

translations.literal: Following on an excursion to Hualin Garden, at his seat he presented lauds to the wind-indicating bird, Huaguang Hall, Jingyang Mountain, and the like; the texts were very beautiful, and the Emperor deeply prized and marveled at them.
translations.idiomatic: On an outing to Hualin Garden he presented odes on the wind-vane bird, Huaguang Hall, and Jingyang Mountain. The emperor admired them greatly.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰章。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous title Zhang.

sentences.zh: 子慎嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 業弟藻。

translations.literal: Ye's younger brother was Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger brother was Zao.

sentences.zh: 九年，徵為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was summoned as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (510) he was summoned as junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧元起之在蜀也，崇於聚斂，財貨山積。

translations.literal: Earlier when Deng Yuanqi was in Shu, he was excessive in collection and accumulation; goods and wealth piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Yuanqi had governed Shu, he taxed heavily and amassed wealth in vast quantities.

sentences.zh: 金玉珍帛為一室，名為內藏；

translations.literal: Gold, jade, and precious silks formed one chamber, named the Inner Treasury;
translations.idiomatic: Gold, jade, and precious silks filled one chamber he called the inner treasury;

sentences.zh: 綺縠錦罽為一室，號曰外府。

translations.literal: Fine gauze, brocade, and felts formed one chamber, titled the Outer Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Fine silks, brocades, and felts another, called the outer storehouse.

sentences.zh: 藻以外府賜將帥，內藏歸王府，不有私焉。

translations.literal: Zao gave the outer storehouse to generals and commanders; the inner treasury returned to the princely house—he kept nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zao gave the outer storehouse to his officers and sent the inner treasury to the princely residence, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 及是還朝，輕裝就路。

translations.literal: When this time he returned to court, he took the road with light baggage.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he traveled light, with little baggage.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 藻性謙退，不求聞達，善屬文，尤好古體。

translations.literal: Zao's nature was modest and retiring; he did not seek fame or advancement; he was skilled at composing text and especially loved archaic style.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was modest and sought no fame, yet wrote well and especially favored archaic verse.

sentences.zh: 自非公宴，未嘗妄有所為，縱有小文，成輒棄本。

translations.literal: Unless it was a public banquet, he never casually produced anything; even if he had a small piece of writing, once finished he discarded the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Except at formal feasts he would not compose carelessly; even a short piece, once finished, he threw away.

sentences.zh: 曆雍、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of the two provinces Yong and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yong and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 頻蒞州鎮，人吏咸稱之。

translations.literal: Frequently he came to provincial seats; officials and people all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He held several provincial posts, and officials and commoners alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 推善下人，常如弗及。

translations.literal: He promoted goodness and deferred to others, always as though he did not match them.
translations.idiomatic: He gave credit to others and always acted as if he fell short of them.

sentences.zh: 普通六年，為軍師將軍，與西豐侯正德北侵渦陽，輒班師，為有司奏，免官削爵土。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Putong he was General of the Army Guard and together with the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, invaded Guoyang in the north; he abruptly withdrew the army; impeached by the relevant offices, he was dismissed from office and stripped of noble rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Putong (525) he served as army strategist with Marquis Zhengde of Xifeng on a northern campaign against Guoyang but withdrew without orders. Impeached, he was stripped of office and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 八年，復封爵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，為中軍將軍，太子詹事，出為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he was Central Army General, Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and sent out as Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhongdatong year (531) he became central army general, tutor to the crown prince, and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱其小字，歎曰：「子弟並如迦葉，吾復何憂。」

translations.literal: The Emperor often used his childhood name and sighed: "If all sons and younger brothers were like Kasyapa, what would I have to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often called him by his childhood name Kasyapa and sighed, "If all my sons and brothers were like Kasyapa, what would I have to fear?"

sentences.zh: 入為尚書左僕射，加侍中，固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He entered as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Department, with the additional title of Palace Attendant; he firmly declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the left secretariat with the added rank of palace attendant. He declined firmly, but the emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，遷中衛將軍、開府儀同三司、中書令，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, he was transferred to Central Guard General, granted the ceremonial rank of Grand Master with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and appointed Director of the Central Secretariat; his post as Palace Attendant remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong (539), he was promoted to central guard general, granted grand-master honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and named director of the central secretariat while retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 藻性恬靜，獨處一室，床有膝痕，宗室衣冠莫不楷則。

translations.literal: Zao's nature was quiet and still; he dwelt alone in one room, and his couch bore knee-marks; among the imperial clan none in court dress failed to take him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was calm and retiring, living alone in a single chamber until the knee-marks were worn into his couch; every princely kinsman in court dress looked to him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 常以爵祿太過，每思摒退，門庭閑寂，賓客罕通。

translations.literal: He often considered that rank and salary were excessive and continually thought to withdraw; his gate and courtyard were calm and still, and guests rarely passed.
translations.idiomatic: Believing his rank and stipend too great, he often wished to resign; his halls stayed quiet and few visitors came.

sentences.zh: 簡文尤敬愛之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen especially revered and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen held him in exceptional esteem and affection.

sentences.zh: 自遭家禍，恒布衣蒲席，不食鮮禽，非公庭不聽音樂，武帝每以此稱之。

translations.literal: Since suffering family calamity, he constantly wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, did not eat fresh poultry, and would not listen to music except at the public court; Emperor Wu often praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: After his family's tragedy he wore only coarse cloth and sat on rush mats, forsook fresh meat, and heard music only at court functions—conduct Emperor Wu praised repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 出為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，藻遣世子彧率兵入援。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zao sent his heir You leading troops to enter and aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing revolted, Zao sent his heir You at the head of troops to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 及城開，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the city was opened, he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege lifted, he was made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 侯景遣其儀同蕭邕代之據京口，藻因感氣疾。

translations.literal: Hou Jing sent his Yitong Xiao Yong to replace him and hold Jingkou; Zao therefore contracted a disorder of vital breath.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent his officer Xiao Yong to take over Jingkou in his place; Zao fell ill from distress.

sentences.zh: 或勸奔江北，藻曰：「吾國之台鉉，任寄特隆，既不能誅翦逆賊，正當同死朝廷耳。」

translations.literal: Some urged fleeing to north of the Yangzi; Zao said: "I am the state's pillar, entrusted with exceptional charge; since I cannot extirpate the rebel traitor, I should rightly die with the court.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee north of the Yangzi. Zao said, "I stand among the state's highest ministers with the heaviest charge upon me. Having failed to destroy the rebel, I can only die with the court.

sentences.zh: 因不食而薨。

translations.literal: Thereupon by not eating he passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 藻弟猷，封臨汝侯，為吳興郡守。

translations.literal: Zao's younger brother You was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru and served as Administrator of Wuxing Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's brother You was made Marquis of Linru and governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻，與楚王廟神交，飲至一斛。

translations.literal: His nature was free and unconventional; he kept company with the god of the King of Chu temple, drinking up to one hu.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited by nature, he kept company with the god of the King of Chu shrine and could drink a hu of wine at a sitting.

sentences.zh: 每酹祀，盡歡極醉，神影亦有酒色，所禱必從。

translations.literal: Each time he poured libations in sacrifice, he enjoyed to the full and drank to utmost drunkenness; the god's image also showed the color of wine; whatever he prayed for was always granted.
translations.idiomatic: At every libation he drank to the full until utterly drunk, and the god's image itself seemed flushed with wine; whatever he prayed for was granted.

sentences.zh: 後為益州刺史，侍中，中護軍。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Yi Province, Palace Attendant, and Colonel of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Yi, palace attendant, and colonel of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 時江陽人齊苟兒反，眾十萬攻州城，猷兵糧俱盡，人有異心。

translations.literal: At that time Qi Gou'er of Jiangyang rebelled; his host of a hundred thousand attacked the provincial city; You's troops and grain were both exhausted, and men harbored other thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Gou'er of Jiangyang rebelled with a host of a hundred thousand and besieged the provincial capital, You's forces ran out of arms and grain, and his men began to waver.

sentences.zh: 乃遙禱請救。

translations.literal: Thereupon from afar he prayed requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: He prayed from afar for deliverance.

sentences.zh: 是日有田老逢一騎浴鐵從東方來，問去城幾裏，曰：「百四十」。

translations.literal: That day an old farmer encountered a mounted man in iron armour coming from the east; he asked how many li from the city—said: "One hundred forty."
translations.idiomatic: That day an old farmer met a rider in black iron armor coming from the east and asked how far he was from the city. "One hundred forty li," the rider answered.

sentences.zh: 時日已晡，騎舉矟曰：「後人來，可令之疾馬，欲及日破賊。」

translations.literal: The day had already reached the hour of shen; the rider raised his spear and said: "When those who come after arrive, you may have them spur their horses swiftly; I wish before the sun sets to break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: It was already afternoon when the rider raised his spear and said, "Tell those who follow to ride hard—I mean to break the rebels before sunset.

sentences.zh: 俄有數百騎如風，一騎過請飲，田老問為誰，曰：「吳興楚王來救臨汝侯。」

translations.literal: Presently several hundred riders like wind; one rider passing asked to drink; the old farmer asked who he was—said: "The King of Chu of Wuxing comes to rescue the Marquis of Linru."
translations.idiomatic: Soon hundreds of horsemen swept up like wind. One rider passing asked for wine. When the old farmer asked who they were, he said, "The King of Chu of Wuxing comes to rescue the Marquis of Linru."

sentences.zh: 當此時，廟中請祈無驗。

translations.literal: At this time prayers at the temple had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile prayers at the shrine went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，乃見侍衛土偶皆泥濕如汗者。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, only then were the clay guardian figures seen all muddy and wet as though sweating.
translations.idiomatic: Not until more than ten days later were the temple guardian figures found covered in mud and wet as though they had sweated.

sentences.zh: 是日，猷大破苟兒。

translations.literal: That day You greatly defeated Gou'er.
translations.idiomatic: That same day You routed Gou'er completely.

sentences.zh: 猷在州頗僭濫，客筵內遂有香橙，不置連榻。

translations.literal: You in the province was rather overstepping and wasteful; at guest banquets there even were fragrant oranges; he did not set up connected couches.
translations.idiomatic: In office You lived with princely extravagance—even fragrant oranges appeared at his banquets—and he would not share the long couch with guests.

sentences.zh: 武帝末知之，以此為愆。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu at the end came to know it and took this as fault.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu learned of it only later and held it against him.

sentences.zh: 還都，以憂愧成疾，卒，諡曰靈，以與神交也。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, from worry and shame he formed illness and died; his posthumous name was Ling, because of communion with spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the capital he fell ill from shame and died. His posthumous title Ling ("spiritual") marked his commerce with the gods.

sentences.zh: 韶昔為幼童，庾信愛之，有斷袖之歡，衣食所資，皆信所給。

translations.literal: Shao formerly as a young boy was loved by Yu Xin; they had the pleasure of severed sleeve; clothing and food relied upon were all given by Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shao won the love of Yu Xin; they shared the intimacy called "severed sleeve," and Xin supplied all his clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 遇客，韶亦為信傳酒。

translations.literal: When meeting guests, Shao also poured wine for Xin.
translations.idiomatic: When guests came, Shao would pour wine for Xin as well.

sentences.zh: 後為郢州，信西上江陵，途經江夏，韶接信甚薄，坐青油幕下，引信入宴，坐信別榻，有自矜色。

translations.literal: Later as Governor of Ying, Xin went west upriver to Jiangling and passed through Jiangxia; Shao received Xin very thinly, sitting under a green-oil awning, leading Xin in to banquet, seating Xin on a separate couch, with an air of self-regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao later governed Ying and Xin traveled west to Jiangling by way of Jiangxia, Shao received him coldly. Under a green-oil awning he invited him to feast but seated Xin apart on his own couch, wearing an air of pride.

sentences.zh: 信稍不堪，因酒酣，乃徑上韶床，踐蹋肴饌，直視韶面，謂曰：「官今日形容大異近日。」

translations.literal: Xin gradually could not bear it; as wine grew merry, he went straight onto Shao's couch, trampling the delicacies, looked straight at Shao's face and said: "Your lordship's appearance today differs greatly from recent days.
translations.idiomatic: Xin could bear it no longer. Drunk, he climbed straight onto Shao's couch, trampled the dishes, stared into Shao's face, and said, "Your lordship looks very different today from what you did not long ago.

sentences.zh: 時賓客滿坐，韶甚慚恥。

translations.literal: At the time guests filled the seats; Shao was very ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was full of guests; Shao was deeply humiliated.

sentences.zh: 韶弟駿字德款，善草隸，工文章，晚更習武，膂力絕人，與永安侯確相類。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Jun, courtesy name Dekuan, was skilled at cursive and clerical script, accomplished at literary composition, and in later years further practiced martial arts; his muscular strength surpassed men; he resembled Marquis Que of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's brother Jun, style name Dekuan, excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy and prose, and in later years took up arms as well—his strength was unmatched, much like Marquis Que of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 位尚書殿中郎、超武將軍，封南安侯。

translations.literal: His posts were Director of the Secretariat Palace Section and Super Martial General; enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the palace secretariat and super martial general, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 城陷，為賊任約所禮。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he was treated with courtesy by the rebel Ren Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the rebel Ren Yue treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 謀召鄱陽嗣王範襲約，反為所害。

translations.literal: He plotted to summon Fan, the Heir Prince of Poyang, to strike Yue; instead he was harmed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to bring in Fan the Prince of Poyang to strike Yue, but Yue killed him first.

sentences.zh: 猷弟朗字靖徹，天監五年，例以王子封侯。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Lang, courtesy name Jingche, in the fifth year of Tianjian by precedent as a king's son was enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: You's brother Lang, style name Jingche, received a marquisate in the fifth Tianjian year (506) as was customary for a prince's son.

sentences.zh: 曆太子洗馬，桂州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He served as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, Governor of Gui Province, with added Commander-in-Chief authority.
translations.idiomatic: He served as groom of the heir's household, then governor of Gui with overall military command.

sentences.zh: 性倨而虐，群下患之。

translations.literal: His nature was proud and cruel; those below all suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and cruel by nature, he made his subordinates miserable.

sentences.zh: 記室庾丹以忠諫見害，帝聞之，使於嶺表以功自效。

translations.literal: His recorder Dan was killed for loyal remonstrance; when the Emperor heard, he had Lang go to the Lingnan region to prove himself by merit.
translations.idiomatic: His recorder Yu Dan was killed for frank counsel. When the emperor heard of it, he sent Lang to the far south to redeem himself by service.

sentences.zh: 丹父景休位御史中丞。

translations.literal: Dan's father Jingxiu held the post of Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's father Jingxiu had been censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 丹少有俊才，與伏挺、何子朗俱為周舍所狎。

translations.literal: Dan in youth had outstanding talent; together with Fu Ting and He Zilang he was all treated familiarly by Zhou She.
translations.idiomatic: Dan showed early brilliance and, with Fu Ting and He Zilang, enjoyed the patronage of Zhou She.

sentences.zh: 初景休罷巴東郡頗有資產，丹負錢數百萬，責者填門。

translations.literal: At first when Jingxiu left Badong Commandery he had considerable property; Dan owed money in the millions; creditors filled the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxiu left his post in Badong he had amassed wealth, but Dan ran up debts of millions, and creditors crowded his door.

sentences.zh: 景休怒，不為之償。

translations.literal: Jingxiu was angry and would not repay for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxiu refused in anger to pay them.

sentences.zh: 既而朝賢之丹不之景休，景休悅，乃悉為還之。

translations.literal: Presently court worthies paid calls on Dan but not on Jingxiu; Jingxiu was pleased and then repaid all for him.
translations.idiomatic: When court grandees began calling on Dan but not on Jingxiu, the father was pleased and paid every debt.

sentences.zh: 為建康正，坐事流廣州。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Jiankang; for an offense he was exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jiankang he was banished to Guangzhou for a crime.

sentences.zh: 朗弟明字靖通，少被武帝親愛，封貞陽侯。

translations.literal: Lang's younger brother Ming, courtesy name Jingtong, in youth was loved by Emperor Wu; enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's brother Ming, style name Jingtong, was cherished by Emperor Wu from boyhood and was made Marquis of Zhenyang.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，為豫州刺史，百姓詣闕拜表，言其德政，樹碑於州門內。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was Governor of Yu Province; the people went to the palace to present a memorial praising his virtuous governance, and set up a stele inside the provincial gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Taiqing year (547) he governed Yu. The people petitioned the throne praising his rule, and a monument was erected inside the provincial gate.

sentences.zh: 及碑匠採石出自肥陵，明乃廣營廚帳，多召人物，躬自率領牽至州。

translations.literal: When the stele craftsmen quarried stone from Feiling, Ming then widely prepared kitchen tents, summoned many men, and personally led them hauling to the province.
translations.idiomatic: When stonemasons took stone from Feiling, Ming set up a vast camp of kitchens, gathered a crowd, and personally led them dragging the blocks to the province.

sentences.zh: 識者笑之，曰：「王自立碑，非州人也。」

translations.literal: Those who understood laughed and said: "The prince set up his own stele—he was not the province's people."
translations.idiomatic: The knowing laughed and said, "The prince raised his own monument—not the people of the province."

sentences.zh: 武帝既納侯景，大舉北侵，使南康王會理總兵，明乃拜表求行。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu had accepted Hou Jing and launched a great northern invasion, he had the Prince of Nankang, Huili, command the army; Ming then submitted a memorial requesting to go.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took in Hou Jing and launched a great northern campaign, he put Prince Huili of Nankang in command; Ming petitioned to join the army.

sentences.zh: 固請，乃許之。

translations.literal: He firmly requested; only then was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his request until the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 會理已至宿預，詔改以明代為都督水陸諸軍趣彭城，大圖進取。

translations.literal: Huili had already reached Suyu; an edict changed to have Ming replace him as Commander-in-Chief of all armies by land and water hastening to Pengcheng, with grand design of advancing and taking.
translations.idiomatic: Huili had already reached Suyu when an edict replaced him with Ming as commander of all land and river forces bound for Pengcheng, with grand plans for conquest.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「侯景志清鄴、洛，以雪讎恥。

translations.literal: The instruction said: "Hou Jing's aim is to clear Ye and Luoyang, to wash away the shame of vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: The order read, "Hou Jing aims to recover Ye and Luoyang and wash away the stain of his revenge.

sentences.zh: 其先率大軍，隨機撫定。
