translations.literal: Let him first lead the great army, taking opportunity as it comes to pacify and settle.
translations.idiomatic: Let him march first with the main force and pacify the region as fortune allows.

sentences.zh: 汝等眾軍可止於寒山築堰，引清水以灌彭城。

translations.literal: You hosts of armies may halt at Hanshan and build a dam, drawing clear water to flood Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of you shall halt at Cold Mountain, build a dam, and channel the clear waters to flood Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 大水一泛，孤城自殄，慎勿妄動。」

translations.literal: When the great water spreads once, the lone city will perish of itself; take care not to act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: One flood will drown the lonely fortress without a fight—do not stir rashly.

sentences.zh: 明師次呂梁十八里，作寒山堰以灌彭城，水及於堞，不沒者三板。

translations.literal: Ming's army halted at Liang eighteen li away, made the Hanshan dam to flood Pengcheng; water reached the parapets; only three boards of height remained above.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's army camped eighteen li from Liang, built the Cold Mountain dam to flood Pengcheng, and raised the water to the battlements—only three plank-heights of wall stayed dry.

sentences.zh: 魏遣將慕容紹宗赴救，明謀略不出，號令莫行。

translations.literal: Wei sent the general Murong Shaozong to rush to rescue; Ming's stratagems did not emerge, and orders were not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Murong Shaozong to relieve the city, but Ming devised no strategy and his orders went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 諸將每諮事，輒怒曰：「吾自臨機制變，勿多言。」

translations.literal: Whenever generals consulted on affairs he would angrily say: "I myself at the moment will control and change matters—do not speak much.
translations.idiomatic: When his generals asked counsel he would snap, "I shall adapt as the moment demands—hold your tongues.

sentences.zh: 眾乃各掠居人，明亦不能制，唯禁其一軍無所侵掠。

translations.literal: The hosts then each plundered inhabitants; Ming also could not control them, only forbidding one army from any plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The troops turned to looting the countryside; Ming could not stop them, but kept his own division from taking anything.

sentences.zh: 紹宗至，決堰水，明命將救之，莫肯出。

translations.literal: When Shaozong arrived, he broke the dam water; Ming ordered generals to save it—none would go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaozong arrived he breached the dam. Ming ordered his generals to stop him, but none would move.

sentences.zh: 魏軍轉逼，人情大駭。

translations.literal: Wei troops pressed ever closer; hearts among the men were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei army closed in, panic seized the host.

sentences.zh: 胡貴孫謂趙伯超曰：「不戰何待。」

translations.literal: Hu Guisun said to Zhao Bochao: "If we do not fight, what do we wait for?
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guisun said to Zhao Bochao, "If we will not fight, what are we waiting for?

sentences.zh: 伯超懼不能對。

translations.literal: Bochao was afraid and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao, afraid, had no answer.

sentences.zh: 貴孫乃入陳苦戰，伯超擁眾弗敢救，曰：「與戰必敗，不如全軍早歸。」

translations.literal: Guisun then entered the battle array and fought bitterly; Bochao hugged his host and dared not rescue, saying: "If we fight we are sure to be defeated; better to preserve the whole army and return early.
translations.idiomatic: Guisun charged into the line and fought fiercely. Bochao held his men back and said, "We are doomed if we join—better to save the army and retreat at once.

sentences.zh: 乃使具良馬，載其愛妾自隨。

translations.literal: He then had fine horses prepared, loading his beloved concubine to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: He had swift horses saddled and took his favorite concubine with him.

sentences.zh: 貴孫遂沒。

translations.literal: Guisun then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Guisun was killed.

sentences.zh: 伯超子威方將赴戰，伯超懼其出，使人召之，遂相與南還。

translations.literal: Bochao's son Weifang was about to go to battle; Bochao feared his going out, sent men to summon him, and together they returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Bochao's son Weifang was riding out to fight when Bochao, afraid to lose him, sent men to call him back; father and son fled south together.

sentences.zh: 明醉不能興，眾軍大敗，明見俘執。

translations.literal: Ming was drunk and could not rise; the great army was utterly defeated; Ming was captured and seized.
translations.idiomatic: Ming lay too drunk to rise. The army was shattered and he was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 北人懷其不侵掠，謂之義王。

translations.literal: Northerners cherished that he had not plundered and called him the Righteous Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners, grateful that his troops had not looted, called him the Righteous Prince.

sentences.zh: 及至魏，魏帝引見明及諸將帥，釋其禁，送晉陽。

translations.literal: When they reached Wei, the Wei Emperor summoned Ming and the generals for audience, released his bonds, and sent him to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei the emperor received Ming and his officers, freed him, and sent him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 勃海王高澄禮明甚重，謂曰：「先王與梁主和好十有餘年，聞彼禮佛文，常雲奉為魏主並及先王，此甚是梁主厚意。

translations.literal: Prince Gao Cheng of Bohai treated Ming with great honor and said: "The former king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; hearing his Buddhist ritual texts, he often said he offered them for the Wei ruler and for the former king as well—this is truly the Liang ruler's deep goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gao Cheng of Bohai received Ming with great respect and said, "For more than ten years the former king and your sovereign kept peace. We heard that in his Buddhist dedications the Liang emperor prayed for our ruler and for our late king alike—that was true goodwill.

sentences.zh: 不謂一朝失信，致此紛擾。」

translations.literal: I did not expect that in one morning faith would be lost, bringing this turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought he would break faith overnight and bring on this chaos?

sentences.zh: 因欲與梁通和，使人以明書告武帝，方致書以慰高澄。

translations.literal: Therefore wishing to make peace with Liang, he sent men with a letter from Ming to inform Emperor Wu; only then did Wu send a letter to console Gao Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking peace with Liang, he sent Ming's letter to Emperor Wu; only then did the emperor write back to reassure Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 東魏除明散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei appointed Ming Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei made Ming regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及聞社稷淪蕩，哀泣不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: When he heard the altars of state had fallen into ruin, he wept in grief without ceasing day or night.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the dynasty was lost, he wept without pause day or night.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，齊文宣使送明至梁，並前所獲梁將湛海珍等皆聽從明歸。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, Qi Emperor Wenxuan had Ming sent to Liang, and together with the Liang generals previously captured such as Zhan Haizhen, all were permitted to follow Ming in returning.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei took Jiangling, Qi Emperor Wenxuan sent Ming back to Liang, allowing captured Liang officers such as Zhan Haizhen to return with him.

sentences.zh: 令上党王渙率眾送之。

translations.literal: He ordered Prince Huan of Shangdang to lead the host escorting him.
translations.idiomatic: He put Prince Huan of Shangdang at the head of the escort.

sentences.zh: 是時太尉王僧辯、司空陳霸先在建康，推晉安王方智為太宰、都督中外諸軍事，承制置百官。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Commander Wang Senbian and Minister of Works Chen Baxian were in Jiankang, promoting Prince Fangzhi of Jin'an as Grand Tutor and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, assuming regency to install the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal Wang Senbian and minister of works Chen Baxian were then in Jiankang. They set up Prince Fangzhi of Jin'an as grand tutor and commander of all forces, and provisionally installed the full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 渙軍漸進，明與僧辯書求迎，僧辯不從。

translations.literal: Huan's army gradually advanced; Ming wrote Wang Senbian asking to be welcomed; Senbian did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan's army drew near, Ming wrote Senbian asking to be received inland. Senbian refused.

sentences.zh: 及渙破東關，斬裴之橫，僧辯懼，乃納明。

translations.literal: When Huan broke Dong Pass and beheaded Pei Zhiheng, Senbian feared and then admitted Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan took Dong Pass and killed Pei Zhiheng, Senbian, afraid, finally admitted Ming.

sentences.zh: 於是梁輿東度，齊師北反。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang's imperial carriage went east across the river; Qi troops turned back north.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor crossed the Yangzi eastward as the Qi army withdrew north.

sentences.zh: 三年，子元簡位郢州刺史，卒于官，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: In the third year, his son Yuanjian held the post of Governor of Ying; died in office; posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his son Yuanjian, governor of Ying, died in office and was given the posthumous title Filial.

sentences.zh: 葬將引，柩有聲，議者欲開視。

translations.literal: When the burial was about to be conducted, the bier made sounds; those deliberating wished to open and look.
translations.idiomatic: As the funeral procession was about to set out, sounds came from the coffin. Some urged opening it to look.

sentences.zh: 王妃柳氏曰：「晉文已有前例，不聞開棺。

translations.literal: The princess consort, Lady Liu, said: "Emperor Wen of Jin already had a precedent—one does not hear of opening the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Liu said, "Emperor Wen of Jin set the precedent—no one speaks of opening the coffin.

sentences.zh: 無益亡者之生，徒增生者之痛。」

translations.literal: It would not benefit the dead to live again; it would only add to the living's pain.
translations.idiomatic: It will not restore the dead but only deepen the grief of the living.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They desisted.

sentences.zh: 少子獻嗣。

translations.literal: The youngest son Xian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Xian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 象字世翼，容止閒雅，簡於交遊，事所生母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiang, courtesy name Shiyi, his bearing and deportment were leisurely and refined; he was spare in socializing; in serving his birth mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, style name Shiyi, was graceful in bearing, chose his company sparingly, and was known for devotion to the mother who bore him.

sentences.zh: 位丹陽尹。

translations.literal: His post was Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 象生長深宮，始親庶政，舉無失德，朝廷稱之。

translations.literal: Xiang grew up in the deep palace; when he first personally handled ordinary governance, his actions had no moral lapse; the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the inner palace, he took up public affairs without a misstep, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 再遷湘州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Governor of Xiang Province with added commander authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to governor of Xiang with overall military command.

sentences.zh: 湘州舊多猛獸為暴，及象任州日，四猛獸死于郭外，自此靜息，故老咸稱德政所感。

translations.literal: Xiang Province formerly had many fierce beasts that ravaged; when Xiang held the province, four fierce beasts died outside the outer wall; from then on quiet ceased; elders all called it moved by virtuous governance.
translations.idiomatic: Savage beasts had long ravaged Xiang, but in his first days in office four died outside the wall and the land grew quiet. The elders called it a response to his virtue.

sentences.zh: 歷位太常卿，加侍中，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He passed through the post of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with added Palace Attendant, transferred to Director of the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the court of sacrifices, was made palace attendant, and became director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰敦。

translations.literal: He passed away; posthumous name Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Dun ("sincere").

sentences.zh: 子慥嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 慥字元貞，位元信州刺史，有威惠。

translations.literal: Cao, courtesy name Yuanzhen, held the post of Governor of Yuanxin Province; he had authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Cao, style name Yuanzhen, governed Yuanxin with a balance of sternness and grace.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，赴援台城，遇敕還蕃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he went to aid the terrace city; he encountered an edict to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Taiqing year (548) he marched to relieve the capital but was ordered back to his fief.

sentences.zh: 尋為張纘所構，書報湘東王曰：「河東、桂陽二蕃，掎角欲襲江陵。」

translations.literal: Soon framed by Zhang Zan, he wrote reporting to the Prince of Xiangdong: "The two fiefs Hedong and Guiyang, horns joined, intend to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Zan slandered him with a letter to the Prince of Xiangdong: "The princes of Hedong and Guiyang mean to strike Jiangling in concert.

sentences.zh: 湘東乃水步兼行至荊鎮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong then by water and foot together hastened to the Jing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Xiangdong marched by land and river together to the Jing garrison.

sentences.zh: 慥尚軍江津，不以為意，湘東至，乃召慥，深加慰喻，慥心乃安。

translations.literal: Cao still held his army at Jiangjin and paid no heed; when the Prince of Xiangdong arrived he summoned Cao and comforted him at length, and Cao's heart was then at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Cao kept his army at Jiangjin and thought nothing of it. When the prince of Xiangdong arrived, he summoned Cao, reassured him at length, and Cao's mind was eased.

sentences.zh: 後留止省內，慥心知禍及，遂肆醜言。

translations.literal: Later he was detained within the provincial headquarters; Cao knew calamity was upon him and thereupon let loose vile words.
translations.idiomatic: He was then kept within the provincial compound. Cao knew disaster was coming and began to speak abusively.

sentences.zh: 湘東大怒，付獄殺之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong was greatly angered and handed him to prison to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Xiangdong was furious and had him thrown into prison and executed.

sentences.zh: 四年，武帝詔宏都督諸軍侵魏。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Wu ordered Hong to be commander-in-chief of all armies invading Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (505), Emperor Wu ordered Hong to command all armies in an invasion of Wei.

sentences.zh: 宏以帝之介弟，所領皆器械精新，軍容甚盛，北人以為百數十年所未之有。

translations.literal: Hong, as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, commanded troops whose weapons were all finely new; his martial display was very grand, and northerners said such a thing had not been seen in a hundred-odd years.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's uterine younger brother, Hong led troops with gleaming new arms and a magnificent host; northerners said nothing like it had been seen in more than a century.

sentences.zh: 軍次洛口，前軍克梁城。

translations.literal: The army halted at Luokou; the vanguard took Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at Luokou, and the vanguard captured Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 巨集部分乖方，多違朝制，諸將欲乘勝深入，宏聞魏援近，畏懦不敢進，召諸將欲議旋師。

translations.literal: Hong's divisions were ill disposed and often violated court regulations; the generals wished to press the victory and advance deep, but Hong heard Wei relief was near, grew fearful and dared not advance, and summoned the generals to discuss withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's formations were badly arranged and often broke court rules. His generals wanted to press the advantage and drive deep, but Hong heard Wei reinforcements were near, lost his nerve, and dared not advance; he called his generals to discuss a retreat.

sentences.zh: 呂僧珍曰：「知難而退，不亦善乎。」

translations.literal: Lü Sengzhen said: "To withdraw when you know difficulty awaits—is that not good?
translations.idiomatic: Lü Sengzhen said, "When you see hardship ahead, to pull back—is that not wise?

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「我亦以為然。」

translations.literal: Hong said: "I too think so."
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "I think so too."

sentences.zh: 柳惔曰：「自我大眾所臨，何城不服，何謂難乎？」

translations.literal: Liu Yan said: "Wherever our great host has come, what city has not submitted? What do you call difficulty?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan said, "Wherever our great army has marched, what city has refused to yield? What hardship do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 裴邃曰：「是行也，固敵是求，何難之避？」

translations.literal: Pei Sui said: "This campaign was undertaken to seek the enemy—why avoid difficulty?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Sui said, "We came on this campaign to find the enemy—why shy from hardship?"

sentences.zh: 馬仙琕曰：「王安得亡國之言。

translations.literal: Ma Xianbi said: "Your Highness, how can you utter words worthy of a doomed state?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xianbi said, "My lord, how can you speak like a man presiding over a dying kingdom?

sentences.zh: 天子掃境內以屬王，有前死一尺，無卻生一寸。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has swept the realm within the borders and entrusted it to you: advance a foot and die there; retreat not an inch alive."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has cleared the realm within the borders and entrusted it to you—die a foot forward, not an inch back alive."

sentences.zh: 昌義之怒須盡磔，曰：「呂僧珍可斬也。

translations.literal: Chang Yizhi, his beard bristling with rage, said: "Lü Sengzhen deserves execution!
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi, trembling with rage, said, "Lü Sengzhen ought to be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 豈有百萬之師，輕言可退，何面目得見聖主乎！」

translations.literal: How can an army of a million speak lightly of retreat—and with what face appear before the sage sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: How can a host of a million speak lightly of retreat? What face have we to show the sage sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 朱僧勇、胡辛生拔劍而起曰：「欲退自退，下官當前向取死！」

translations.literal: Zhu Yong and Hu Xinsheng drew their swords and rose, saying: "Those who wish to retreat may retreat; this subordinate will advance and seek death!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yong and Hu Xinsheng drew their swords and stood up. "Let those who want to retreat retreat," they said. "I will go forward and die!"

sentences.zh: 議者已罷，僧珍謝諸將曰：「殿下昨來風動，意不在軍，深恐大致沮喪，欲使全師而反。」

translations.literal: When the council had ended, Sengzhen apologized to the generals, saying: "Your Highness yesterday seemed swayed by the wind; his mind was not on the army. I deeply feared morale would collapse utterly and wished to bring the whole host back intact."
translations.idiomatic: When the meeting broke up, Sengzhen apologized to the generals. "Yesterday His Highness seemed unsteady," he said, "his mind not on the army. I feared morale would collapse and wanted to bring the whole force back intact."

sentences.zh: 又私裴邃曰：「王非止全無經略，庸怯過甚。

translations.literal: In private he said to Pei Sui: "The prince is not only wholly without strategy—his mediocrity and cowardice exceed all bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he told Pei Sui, "The prince lacks not only strategy—his dullness and cowardice are beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 吾與言軍事，都不相入。

translations.literal: When I speak with him of military affairs, nothing penetrates.
translations.idiomatic: When I discuss military matters with him, nothing I say gets through.

sentences.zh: 觀此形勢，豈能成功。」

translations.literal: Judging by this situation, how can we succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Looking at this situation, how can we succeed?"

sentences.zh: 宏不敢便違群議，停軍不前。

translations.literal: Hong dared not openly defy the joint counsel and halted the army without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Hong did not dare openly defy the consensus and kept the army halted without advancing.

sentences.zh: 魏人知其不武，遺以巾幗。

translations.literal: The Wei, knowing him unwarlike, sent him women's kerchiefs and skirts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei, knowing he was no warrior, sent him women's headcloths and skirts.

sentences.zh: 北軍歌曰：「不畏蕭娘與呂姥，但畏合肥有韋武。」

translations.literal: A northern song ran: "We fear not the Xiao girl and the Lü crone, but only Wei's martial prowess at Hefei."
translations.idiomatic: A northern camp song ran, "We fear not the Xiao lass and the Lü hag, but only Wei the warrior at Hefei."

sentences.zh: 武謂韋叡也。

translations.literal: Wu" refers to Wei Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu" means Wei Rui.

sentences.zh: 僧珍歎曰：「使始興、吳平為元帥，我相毗輔，中原不足平。

translations.literal: Sengzhen sighed: "Had the princes of Shixing and Wu Ping been commanders with me to support them, the central plains would have been no great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzhen sighed, "If the princes of Shixing and Wu Ping had been commanders and I had aided them, the central plains would not have been hard to pacify.

sentences.zh: 今遂敵人見欺如此。」

translations.literal: Now we are mocked by the enemy thus.
translations.idiomatic: Now we are ridiculed by the enemy like this.

sentences.zh: 乃欲遣裴邃分軍取壽陽，大眾停洛口。

translations.literal: He wished to send Pei Sui with a detached force to take Shouyang while the main body remained at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to send Pei Sui with a separate force to take Shouyang while the main army stayed at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 宏固執不聽，乃令軍中曰：「人馬有前行者斬。」

translations.literal: Hong obstinately refused to listen and ordered throughout the army: "Whoever advances, man or horse, shall be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Hong stubbornly refused and issued an army order: "Any man or horse that moves forward will be executed.

sentences.zh: 自是軍政不和，人懷憤怒。

translations.literal: From then on civil and military were at odds, and the men harbored anger.
translations.idiomatic: After that, civil and military affairs fell out of harmony and the troops seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 魏奚康生馳遣楊大眼謂元英曰：「梁人自克梁城已後，久不進軍，其勢可見，當是懼我。

translations.literal: The Wei general Xi Kangsheng galloped to send Yang Dayan to Yuan Ying, saying: "Since the Liang men took Liangcheng they have long not advanced; their condition is plain—they must fear us.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei general Xi Kangsheng rode posthaste to send Yang Dayan to Yuan Ying. "Since the Liang took Liangcheng they have not advanced for a long time," he said. "Their situation is clear—they must fear us.

sentences.zh: 王若進據洛水，彼自奔敗。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness advances and holds the Luo River, they will flee in defeat of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If you advance and seize the Luo River, they will break and flee on their own.

sentences.zh: 元英曰：「蕭臨川雖騃，其下有好將韋、裴之屬，亦未可當。

translations.literal: Yuan Ying said: "Although the Prince of Linchuan is dull, beneath him are fine generals such as Wei and Pei—not to be lightly met.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ying said, "Though the prince of Linchuan is slow-witted, he has fine generals below him—men like Wei and Pei—and cannot be taken lightly.

sentences.zh: 望氣者言九月賊退，今且觀形勢，未可便與交鋒。」

translations.literal: Physiognomists say the rebels will withdraw in the ninth month; for now observe the situation—we cannot yet join battle."
translations.idiomatic: Men who read the omens say the rebels will withdraw in the ninth month. For now watch how things stand—we cannot yet join battle."

sentences.zh: 張惠紹次下邳，號令嚴明，所至獨克，下邳人多有欲來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Huishao encamped at Xiapi; his orders were strict and bright, and where he went he alone prevailed; many in Xiapi wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huishao camped at Xiapi. His discipline was strict and wherever he went he alone prevailed. Many in Xiapi wanted to surrender.

sentences.zh: 惠紹曰：「我若得城，諸卿皆是國人；

translations.literal: Huishao said: "If I take the city, you all will be countrymen alike;
translations.idiomatic: Huishao said, "If I take the city, you will all be our countrymen again;

sentences.zh: 若不能破賊，徒令公等失鄉，非朝廷吊人本意也。

translations.literal: if we cannot defeat the bandits, we would only make you lose your homes—this is not the court's intent in comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: if we cannot defeat the enemy, we would only make you lose your homes—and that is not what the court means by bringing comfort to the people.

sentences.zh: 今且安堵復業，勿妄自辛苦。」

translations.literal: For now settle in peace and resume your trades; do not labor yourselves in vain.
translations.idiomatic: For now live in peace and return to your work. Do not trouble yourselves needlessly.

sentences.zh: 降人咸悅。

translations.literal: The surrendering people were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had wanted to surrender were all pleased.

sentences.zh: 九月，洛口軍潰，宏棄眾走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army at Luokou collapsed; Hong abandoned his troops and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army at Luokou collapsed. Hong abandoned his troops and fled.

sentences.zh: 其夜暴風雨，軍驚，宏與數騎逃亡。

translations.literal: That night a violent storm arose; the army panicked, and Hong fled with a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: That night a violent storm broke. The army panicked, and Hong fled with only a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 諸將求宏不得，眾散而歸。

translations.literal: The generals sought Hong but could not find him; the host scattered and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The generals searched for Hong but could not find him. The army scattered and went home.

sentences.zh: 棄甲投戈，填滿水陸，捐棄病者，強壯僅得脫身。

translations.literal: Cast-off armor and thrown spears filled land and water; the sick were abandoned, and only the strong barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Discarded armor and spears choked the roads and waterways. The sick were left behind; only the strong barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 宏乘小船濟江，夜至白石壘，款城門求入。

translations.literal: Hong took a small boat across the Yangzi and by night reached the Baishi fortress, knocking at the gate to be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hong crossed the Yangzi in a small boat and reached the Baishi fortress at night, knocking at the gate to be let in.

sentences.zh: 臨汝侯登城謂曰：「百萬之師，一朝奔潰，國之存亡，未可知也。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Linru climbed the wall and said: "An army of a million collapsed in a morning; the state's survival is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis of Linru mounted the wall and said, "An army of a million collapsed in a single morning. Whether the state survives is not yet known.

sentences.zh: 恐奸人乘間為變，城門不可夜開。」

translations.literal: I fear villains may seize the moment to make trouble—the gate cannot be opened at night.
translations.idiomatic: I fear troublemakers may seize the moment to make mischief. The gate cannot be opened at night.

sentences.zh: 宏無辭以對，乃縋食饋之。

translations.literal: Hong had no reply and could only lower food to feed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had nothing to say in reply. They lowered food down to him on a rope.

sentences.zh: 惠紹聞洛口敗，亦退軍。

translations.literal: When Huishao heard of the defeat at Luokou, he too withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huishao heard of the defeat at Luokou, he too pulled his army back.

sentences.zh: 宏妾弟吳法壽性粗狡，恃宏無所畏忌，輒殺人。

translations.literal: Hong's concubine's younger brother Wu Fashou was crude and cunning by nature; relying on Hong he feared nothing and would kill people at will.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fashou, younger brother of Hong's concubine, was coarse and cunning by nature. Trusting in Hong's protection, he feared nothing and killed people as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 死家訴，有敕嚴討。

translations.literal: The bereaved families sued; an edict ordered severe pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The victims' families brought suit, and an edict ordered a strict investigation.

sentences.zh: 法壽在宏府內，無如之何。

translations.literal: Fashou was inside Hong's mansion and nothing could be done.
translations.idiomatic: Fashou stayed inside Hong's mansion, and no one could touch him.

sentences.zh: 武帝制宏出之，即日償辜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu commanded Hong to hand him over; that same day atonement was made.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered Hong to hand him over. That same day the debt of blood was paid.

sentences.zh: 南司奏免宏司徒、驃騎、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: The southern bureau memorialized to remove Hong from his posts of Director of the Secretariat, Cavalry-in-Chief, and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The southern bureau memorialized to strip Hong of his titles as director of the secretariat, cavalry-in-chief, and governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝注曰：「愛巨集者兄弟私親，免宏者王者正法，所奏可。」

translations.literal: The emperor annotated: "To love Hong is a brother's private affection; to dismiss Hong is the king's public law. The memorial is approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in the margin, "To love Hong is a brother's private feeling; to dismiss him is the king's public law. The memorial is approved."

sentences.zh: 宏自洛口之敗，常懷愧憤，都下每有竊發，輒以宏為名，屢為有司所奏，帝每貰之。

translations.literal: After his defeat at Luokou Hong constantly nursed shame and resentment; whenever theft broke out in the capital it was attributed to Hong, and he was repeatedly reported by the authorities, but the emperor each time pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Luokou Hong brooded on shame and anger. Whenever a theft occurred in the capital it was blamed on Hong. Officials reported him again and again, but the emperor pardoned him each time.

sentences.zh: 十七年，帝將幸光宅寺，有士伏於驃騎航待帝夜出。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the emperor was about to visit Guangzai Temple, a man lay in wait at the Piaoqi crossing for the emperor's night exit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when the emperor was about to visit Guangzai Temple, a man lay in ambush at the Piaoqi crossing, waiting for the emperor to pass by night.

sentences.zh: 帝將行心動，乃於朱雀航過。

translations.literal: As the emperor was about to go his heart stirred, and he passed by way of the Zhuque crossing instead.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to set out, his heart misgave him, and he went by the Zhuque crossing instead.

sentences.zh: 事發，稱為宏所使。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered, it was said Hong had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was uncovered, it was said Hong had sent the man.

sentences.zh: 帝泣謂宏曰：「我人才勝汝百倍，當此猶恐顛墜，汝何為者。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said to Hong: "My talent surpasses yours a hundredfold, yet even so I fear a fall—what are you doing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said to Hong, "My ability surpasses yours a hundredfold, yet even I fear a fall in such moments—what are you doing?

sentences.zh: 我非不能為周公、漢文，念汝愚故。」

translations.literal: It is not that I cannot act like the Duke of Zhou or Emperor Wen of Han—I think of your folly.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I cannot act like the Duke of Zhou or Emperor Wen of Han. I spare you because you are a fool.

sentences.zh: 宏頓首曰：「無是，無是。」

translations.literal: Hong kowtowed and said: "It is not so, it is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Hong kowtowed and said, "No, no—it is not so."

sentences.zh: 於是以罪免。

translations.literal: On that account he was cleared of the charge.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he was cleared of the crime.

sentences.zh: 而縱恣不悛，奢侈過度，修第擬于帝宮，後庭數百千人，皆極天下之選。

translations.literal: Yet he was unrestrained and unrepentant, extravagant beyond measure; his mansion rivaled the imperial palace, and his rear apartments held several hundred persons, all the finest selections under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he grew no more restrained. His extravagance knew no limit: his mansion rivaled the imperial palace, and his inner quarters held several hundred people, each the finest the realm could offer.

sentences.zh: 所幸江無畏服玩侔于齊東昏潘妃，寶屧直千萬。

translations.literal: His favorite Jiang Wujie—robes and playthings rivaled those of the Qi consort Pan of the Eastern Depraved; jeweled slippers were worth ten million.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite, Jiang Wujie, dressed and played at finery to rival Consort Pan of the Eastern Qi. Her jeweled slippers were worth ten million.

sentences.zh: 好食鰿魚頭，常日進三百，其佗珍膳盈溢，後房食之不盡，棄諸道路。

translations.literal: He loved to eat globefish heads—three hundred were served daily; other rare delicacies overflowed. The rear apartments could not finish them, and they were cast upon the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He loved globefish heads—three hundred were served every day. Other rare delicacies overflowed the kitchens. His inner quarters could not consume them all, and the surplus was thrown into the streets.

sentences.zh: 江本吳氏女也，世有國色，親從子女遍游王侯後宮，男免兄弟九人，因權勢橫於都下。

translations.literal: Jiang was originally a woman of the Wu clan, famed for beauty in her generation; her kin and children roamed the inner palaces of princes and marquises; nine brothers on the male side, through their power, swaggered through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang was a Wu-clan woman of celebrated beauty. Her kin and children moved freely through princes' and marquises' inner quarters. Nine brothers on her side swaggered through the capital on her influence.

sentences.zh: 宏未幾復為司徒。

translations.literal: Before long Hong was again made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hong was made director of the secretariat again.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，遷太尉、揚州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he was transferred to Grand Marshal and Governor of Yangzhou, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Putong year (520) he was promoted to grand marshal and governor of Yangzhou, retaining his post as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 七年四月薨，自疾至薨，輿駕七出臨視。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the seventh year he died; from illness to death the imperial carriage came seven times to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of the seventh year (526). From the onset of illness until his death the emperor's carriage came seven times to visit him.

sentences.zh: 及薨，詔贈侍中、大將軍、揚州牧，假黃鉞，並給羽葆、鼓吹一部，增班劍為六十人，諡曰靖惠。

translations.literal: Upon his death an edict enfeoffed him posthumously as Palace Attendant, Grand General, and Governor of Yangzhou, with the yellow battle-axe bestowed, and granted feather banners and a full set of martial pipes; guard swords were increased to sixty; posthumous title Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: After his death an edict posthumously made him palace attendant, grand general, and governor of Yangzhou, with the yellow battle-axe granted, a feather canopy and martial pipes supplied, and his guard of swords raised to sixty. His posthumous title was Jinghui (Tranquil and Gracious).

sentences.zh: 宏以介弟之貴，無佗量能，恣意聚斂。

translations.literal: Hong, by the eminence of a younger brother of the same mother, had no other capacity and amassed wealth at will.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, elevated as the emperor's uterine younger brother, had no other talent and hoarded wealth as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 庫室垂有百間，在內堂之後，關鑰甚嚴。

translations.literal: Treasury rooms nearly a hundred in number stood behind the inner hall, locked with the strictest keys.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a hundred treasury rooms stood behind the inner hall, locked with the strictest care.

sentences.zh: 有疑是鎧仗者，密以聞。

translations.literal: Someone suspected they held armor and weapons and reported secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Someone suspected they held armor and weapons and reported it in secret.

sentences.zh: 武帝于友于甚厚，殊不悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was exceedingly devoted to fraternal feeling and was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished brotherly feeling deeply and was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 宏愛妾江氏寢膳不能暫離，上佗日送盛饌與江曰：「當來就汝歡宴。」

translations.literal: Hong's beloved concubine Lady Jiang could not leave his bed and board even briefly. On another day the emperor sent a sumptuous meal to Jiang, saying: "I shall come to share your joyful banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's beloved concubine Lady Jiang would not leave his bed and board even for a moment. On another day the emperor sent a lavish meal to Jiang with the message, "I shall come feast with you in joy.

sentences.zh: 唯攜布衣之舊射聲校尉丘佗卿往，與宏及江大飲，半醉後謂曰：「我今欲履行汝後房。」

translations.literal: Taking only his old companion in plain cloth, Commandant of Archers Qiu Tuqing, he went and drank heavily with Hong and Jiang; half drunk he said: "I wish now to walk through your rear apartments."
translations.idiomatic: He took only his old friend in plain dress, Commandant of Archers Qiu Tuqing, and went to drink heavily with Hong and Jiang. Half drunk, he said, "Today I mean to walk through your rear apartments."

sentences.zh: 便呼後合輿徑往屋所。

translations.literal: He then called for the rear palanquin and went straight to the storerooms.
translations.idiomatic: He called for the rear palanquin and went straight to the storerooms.

sentences.zh: 宏恐上見其賄貨，顏色怖懼。

translations.literal: Hong feared the emperor would see his bribes and goods; his face showed terror.
translations.idiomatic: Hong feared the emperor would see his hoarded goods. His face went pale with terror.

sentences.zh: 上意彌信是仗，屋屋檢視。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind believed them all the more to be arms; room by room he inspected.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was all the more convinced they held weapons and inspected room after room.

sentences.zh: 宏性愛錢，百萬一聚，黃牓標之，千萬一庫，懸一紫標，如此三十餘間。

translations.literal: Hong was by nature fond of money: a million at a pile with a yellow placard, ten million a storehouse with a purple marker—thus for more than thirty rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Hong loved money by nature. Each pile of a million had a yellow label; each storehouse of ten million bore a purple tag—more than thirty rooms in all.

sentences.zh: 帝與佗卿屈指計見錢三億余萬，餘屋貯布絹絲綿漆蜜紵蠟朱沙黃屑雜貨，但見滿庫，不知多少。

translations.literal: The emperor and Tuqing counted on their fingers and saw cash exceeding three hundred million; other rooms held cloth, silk, floss, lacquer, honey, ramie, wax, cinnabar, yellow ore, and sundry goods—storehouses full, the quantity unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Tuqing reckoned on their fingers and found more than three hundred million in coin. Other rooms held cloth, silk, floss, lacquer, honey, ramie, wax, cinnabar, yellow ore, and miscellaneous goods—storehouse after storehouse full, with no counting the total.

sentences.zh: 帝始知非仗，大悅，謂曰：「阿六，汝生活大可。」

translations.literal: The emperor then knew it was not arms and was greatly pleased, saying: "Ah, Sixth Brother, your means of living are ample indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then knew they were not weapons and was greatly pleased. "Ah, Sixth Brother," he said, "you live well indeed.

sentences.zh: 方更劇飲，至夜舉燭而還。

translations.literal: They drank all the more heavily until night, returning by torchlight.
translations.idiomatic: They drank all the harder until nightfall and returned by torchlight.

sentences.zh: 兄弟情方更敦睦。

translations.literal: Brotherly feeling grew still more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers' affection grew warmer still.

sentences.zh: 宏都下有數十邸出懸錢立券，每以田宅邸店懸上文券，期訖便驅券主，奪其宅。

translations.literal: Hong had several dozen loan offices in the capital posting credit and bonds; he would hang deeds on houses and shops as collateral, and when the term ended drive off the bondholders and seize their properties.
translations.idiomatic: Hong ran several dozen money offices in the capital that posted loans and bonds. He would register houses and shops on the loan documents, and when the term expired he drove off the creditors and seized the property.

sentences.zh: 都下東土百姓，失業非一。

translations.literal: Common folk of eastern soil in the capital lost their livelihoods—not a few.
translations.idiomatic: Common people from the eastern provinces in the capital lost their livelihoods—more than a few.

sentences.zh: 帝后知，制懸券不得復驅奪，自此後貧庶不復失居業。

translations.literal: When emperor and empress learned of it, they decreed that hanging bonds could no longer justify seizure, and from then the poor no longer lost their homes and trades.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and empress learned of it, they decreed that posted bonds could no longer be used to seize property. After that the poor no longer lost their homes and livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 晉時有錢神論，豫章王綜以宏貪吝，遂為錢愚論，其文甚切。

translations.literal: In Jin times there had been "On the Money God"; Prince Zong of Yuzhang, because Hong was greedy and stingy, wrote "On the Money Fool," its text very pointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times there had been an essay "On the Money God." Prince Zong of Yuzhang, finding Hong greedy and miserly, wrote "On the Money Fool," its language sharp.

sentences.zh: 帝知以激宏，宣旨與綜：「天下文章何限，那忽作此？」

translations.literal: The emperor knew it was to provoke Hong and issued a decree to Zong: "Articles under heaven are without limit—why suddenly compose this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew it was meant to goad Hong and sent word to Zong, "Essays in the world are without number—why write this one?

sentences.zh: 雖令急毀，而流布已遠，宏深病之，聚斂稍改。

translations.literal: Though he ordered it destroyed at once, it had already spread far; Hong was deeply wounded and moderated his hoarding somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Though he ordered it destroyed at once, the piece had already spread far and wide. Hong was deeply stung and moderated his hoarding somewhat.

sentences.zh: 宏又與帝女永興主私通，因是遂謀弑逆，許事捷以為皇后。

translations.literal: Hong also carried on an affair with the emperor's daughter Princess Yongxing; on that account he plotted regicide, promising that when the deed succeeded she would be made empress.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also had a secret affair with the emperor's daughter Princess Yongxing. On that account he plotted regicide, promising that if the deed succeeded she would become empress.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗為三日齋，諸主並豫，永興乃使二僮衣以婢服。

translations.literal: Once when the emperor observed a three-day fast, all princesses attended; Yongxing sent two boy servants dressed as maids.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor kept a three-day fast, all the princesses attended. Yongxing sent two boy servants dressed as maids.

sentences.zh: 僮踰閾失屨，合帥疑之，密言于丁貴嬪，欲上言懼或不信，乃使宮帥圖之。

translations.literal: A servant crossed the threshold and lost a shoe; the duty officer grew suspicious and spoke secretly to Consort Ding. He wished to report upward but feared he might not be believed, and so had the palace marshal sketch them.
translations.idiomatic: One servant crossed the threshold and lost a shoe. The duty officer grew suspicious and told Consort Ding in secret. He wanted to report it but feared he would not be believed, so he had the palace marshal draw their likenesses.

sentences.zh: 帥令內輿人八人，纏以純綿，立於幕下。

translations.literal: The marshal ordered eight inner palanquin bearers wrapped in pure cotton and posted them beneath the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal ordered eight inner palanquin bearers wrapped in padded cotton and stationed them beneath the curtain.

sentences.zh: 齋坐散，主果請間，帝許之。

translations.literal: When the fast gathering dispersed, the princess indeed asked for a private audience and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the fast ended and the assembly broke up, the princess asked for a private audience, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 主升階，而僮先趣帝后。

translations.literal: As the princess ascended the steps, the servants rushed ahead toward the emperor and empress.
translations.idiomatic: As the princess mounted the steps, the servants ran ahead toward the emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 八人抱而擒之，帝驚墜於扆。

translations.literal: The eight men seized and held them; the emperor started and fell against the screen.
translations.idiomatic: The eight men seized them. The emperor started in shock and fell against the screen-frame.

sentences.zh: 搜僮得刀，辭為宏所使。

translations.literal: Searching the servants they found knives; under interrogation they said Hong had sent them.
translations.idiomatic: A search of the servants turned up knives. Under questioning they said Hong had sent them.

sentences.zh: 帝秘之，殺二僮於內，以漆車載主出。

translations.literal: The emperor kept it secret, executed the two servants within, and had the princess borne out in a lacquered carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept the matter secret, executed the two servants within the palace, and had the princess carried out in a lacquered carriage.

sentences.zh: 主恚死，帝竟不臨之。

translations.literal: The princess died of rage; the emperor in the end did not visit her bier.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died of shame and rage. The emperor never went to mourn her.

sentences.zh: 帝諸女臨安、安吉、長城三主並有文才，而安吉最得令稱。

translations.literal: Of the emperor's daughters, the princesses of Lin'an, Anji, and Changcheng all had literary talent, but Anji won the finest reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Among the emperor's daughters, the princesses of Lin'an, Anji, and Changcheng all had literary gifts, but Anji won the finest name.

sentences.zh: 宏性好內樂酒，沈湎聲色，侍女千人，皆極綺麗。

translations.literal: Hong by nature loved the inner quarters and delighted in wine; he drowned himself in sensual pleasures. His serving girls numbered a thousand, all of surpassing splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was devoted to the inner quarters and fond of wine, lost in music and women. He kept a thousand maidservants, every one of them ravishing.

sentences.zh: 慎衛寡方，故屢致降免。

translations.literal: In caution he guarded himself but lacked proper restraint; therefore he repeatedly incurred demotion and removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Though he tried to be careful, he lacked self-discipline, and was repeatedly demoted and stripped of his posts.

sentences.zh: 宏子十人許，可知者七人，長子正仁字公業，位秘書丞，早卒，諡哀世子。

translations.literal: Hong had some ten sons; seven are known. The eldest son Zhengren, courtesy name Gongye, held the post of Secretary Palace Aid; he died young and was posthumously titled Lamented Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had about ten sons, of whom seven are recorded. The eldest, Zhengren (Gongye), served as Secretary Palace Aid. He died young and was posthumously titled Lamented Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 正仁弟正義嗣。

translations.literal: Zhengren's younger brother Zhengyi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengren's younger brother Zhengyi succeeded to his place.

sentences.zh: 正德字公和，少而凶慝，招聚亡命，破塚屠牛，兼好弋獵。

translations.literal: Zhengde, courtesy name Gonghe, from youth was fierce and wicked; he gathered fugitives, broke tombs and slaughtered cattle, and was likewise fond of archery and hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde (Gonghe) was vicious from boyhood. He gathered outlaws, opened graves, butchered cattle, and loved the bow and the hunt.

sentences.zh: 齊建武中，武帝胤嗣未立，養以為子。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi, Emperor Wu's heir had not yet been established; he adopted [Zhengde] as his son.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi's Jianwu era, before Emperor Wu had named an heir, he adopted Zhengde as his son.

sentences.zh: 及平建康，生昭明太子，正德還本。

translations.literal: When [the Liang] pacified Jiankang and the Heir Apparent Zhaoming was born, Zhengde returned to his original status.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Jiankang, when the Heir Apparent Zhaoming was born, Zhengde reverted to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 天監初，封西豐縣侯，累遷吳郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng and rose in succession to Governor of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianjian reign, he was made Marquis of Xifeng and eventually became Governor of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 正德自謂應居儲嫡，心常怏怏，每形於言。

translations.literal: Zhengde considered that he ought to hold the position of legitimate heir; his heart was ever resentful, and he showed it in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde believed he should have been heir. He brooded on it constantly and let his bitterness show in what he said.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，以黃門侍郎為輕車將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong, from Gentleman at the Yellow Gate he was made General of the Light Chariot, with staff and clerks appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year three (520) he was promoted from Gentleman at the Yellow Gate to General of the Light Chariot, with his own staff and clerks.

sentences.zh: 頃之奔魏。

translations.literal: Before long he fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he defected to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 初去之始，為詩一絕，內火籠中，即詠竹火籠，曰：「楨幹屈曲盡，蘭麝氛氳銷，欲知懷炭日，正是履冰朝。」

translations.literal: At the very outset of his departure he composed one quatrain; within a brazier he at once chanted on a bamboo brazier, saying: "Trunks and branches all bent to the end, orchid and musk fragrant vapor spent — if you would know the day one cherishes embers, it is precisely the morning one treads on ice."
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving he wrote a four-line poem. Sitting by an inner brazier, he improvised verses on a bamboo hand-warmer: "The frame is bent through and through, the scent of orchid and musk all gone — if you wish to know the day you warm yourself by coals, it is the very morning you walk on ice.

sentences.zh: 至魏稱是被廢太子。

translations.literal: Reaching Wei he declared that he had been a deposed crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he claimed that he had been the deposed crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時齊蕭寶寅先在魏，乃上表魏帝曰：「豈有伯為天子，父作揚州，棄彼密親，遠投佗國。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Baoyin of Qi was already in Wei; he submitted a memorial to the Wei emperor, saying: "How can it be that an elder brother is Son of Heaven while his father serves as governor of Yangzhou, yet abandons those close in blood and flees far to another state?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin of Qi was already in Wei at the time. He memorialized the Wei emperor: "How can a man flee to a foreign realm when his brother is emperor and his father governs Yangzhou? He has cast off his own kin.

sentences.zh: 不若殺之。」

translations.literal: It would be better to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Better to kill him.

sentences.zh: 魏既不禮之，正德乃殺一小兒稱為己子，遠營葬地，魏人不疑，又自魏逃歸。

translations.literal: Wei did not treat him with ceremony; Zhengde then killed a small child and called it his own son, far off arranged a burial ground, and the people of Wei did not suspect. Again he escaped from Wei and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei showed him no honor, Zhengde killed a small boy and passed the body off as his own son, arranging a distant funeral so the Wei court would not suspect him — then he escaped back to Liang.

sentences.zh: 見於文德殿，至庭叩頭。

translations.literal: He appeared at the Wende Hall and, reaching the court, kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself at the Wende Hall and kowtowed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 武帝泣而誨之，特復本封。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu wept as he admonished him and specially restored his original fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wept as he reproached him, then restored his original title and lands.

sentences.zh: 正德志行無悛，常公行剝掠。

translations.literal: Zhengde's will and conduct showed no repentance; he often openly went about plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde showed no repentance at all and openly robbed as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 時東府有正德及樂山侯正則；

translations.literal: At that time in the Eastern Quarter were Zhengde and the Marquis of Leshan Zhengze;
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Quarter at that time were Zhengde and Zhengze, Marquis of Leshan;

sentences.zh: 潮溝有董當門子暹，世謂之董世子者也；

translations.literal: along Chaogou was Xuan, son of Dong Dang's household, whom the age called Master Dong's son;
translations.idiomatic: along the Chaogou Canal lived Xuan, son of the Dong household — known everywhere as "the Dong heir";

sentences.zh: 南岸有夏侯夔世子洪。

translations.literal: on the south bank was Hong, heir son of Xiahou Kui.
translations.idiomatic: on the south bank was Hong, heir of Xiahou Kui.

sentences.zh: 此四凶者，為百姓巨蠹，多聚亡命，黃昏多殺人於道，謂之「打稽」。

translations.literal: These four villains were a great blight on the common people, gathering many fugitives; at dusk they often killed people on the roads — called "beating the guard."
translations.idiomatic: These four villains were a plague on the people. They gathered gangs of outlaws and murdered travelers at dusk in a practice they called "beating the guard."

sentences.zh: 時勳豪子弟多縱恣，以淫盜屠殺為業，父祖不能制，尉邏莫能禦。

translations.literal: At the time sons and brothers of meritorious and powerful families mostly gave free rein to their passions, making debauchery, robbery, and slaughter their trade; fathers and grandfathers could not restrain them, nor could patrol guards repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of the great clans ran wild across the capital, turning rape, theft, and murder into sport. Their fathers could not control them, and the night watch could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 車服牛馬，號西豐駱馬，樂山烏牛。

translations.literal: For carriage, dress, cattle, and horses they were called Xifeng's Bactrian camels and Leshan's black cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Their carriages, horses, and retinues were famed as "Xifeng's Bactrian camels" and "Leshan's black oxen."

sentences.zh: 董暹金帖織成戰襖，直七百萬。

translations.literal: Dong Xuan's battle jacket of gold-inlaid brocade was worth seven million.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xuan wore a battle jacket of gold-thread brocade worth seven million cash.

sentences.zh: 後正則為劫，殺沙門，徙嶺南死。

translations.literal: Later Zhengze committed robbery and killed a Buddhist monk; he was banished to Lingnan and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengze was later caught in robbery and killed a monk; he was exiled to Lingnan and died there.

sentences.zh: 洪為其父夔奏系東冶，死於徒。

translations.literal: Hong was imprisoned in the Eastern Forge by his father Kui's memorial; he died in corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's father Kui had him imprisoned in the Eastern Forge; he died on the works gang.

sentences.zh: 暹坐與永陽王妃王氏亂，誅。

translations.literal: Xuan was punished for debauchery with the princess consort of Yongyang, née Wang, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was executed for carrying on an affair with the princess consort of Yongyang, Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 三人既除，百姓少安。

translations.literal: Once the three men were removed, the common people knew a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: After these three were removed, the common people breathed a little easier.

sentences.zh: 正德淫虐不革，尋除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhengde's debauchery and cruelty underwent no change; before long he was again made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde's depravity never changed. Soon he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate again.

sentences.zh: 六年為輕車將軍，隨豫章王北侵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became General of the Light Chariot and followed the Prince of Yuzhang in the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became General of the Light Chariot and joined the Prince of Yuzhang's northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 正德輒棄軍委走，為有司所奏下獄。

translations.literal: Zhengde abruptly abandoned the army and fled; the responsible officials memorialized and he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde deserted his command and fled. The authorities reported him and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 帝復詔曰：「汝以猶子，情兼常愛，故越先汝兄，剖符連郡。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an edict, saying: "As my adopted son, your affection stands apart from the ordinary; therefore, ahead of your elder brothers, I enfeoffed you with linked commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued another edict: "As my adopted son you held a special place in my heart — that is why I enfeoffed you before your elder brothers and gave you commanderies in succession.

sentences.zh: 往年在蜀，昵近小人，猶謂少年情志未定。

translations.literal: In former years in Shu you kept company with petty men; I still said it was the unfixed passion of youth.
translations.idiomatic: Years ago in Shu you consorted with riffraff, and I told myself it was the recklessness of youth.

sentences.zh: 更于吳郡殺戮無辜，劫盜財物，雅然無畏。

translations.literal: Again in Wu Commandery you slaughtered the innocent and robbed property, with natural fearlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Then in Wu you slaughtered innocents and plundered property as boldly as if you owned the roads.

sentences.zh: 及還京師，專為逋逃，乃至江乘要道，湖頭斷路，遂使京邑士女，早閉晏開。

translations.literal: When you returned to the capital you specialized in sheltering fugitives, even on the vital route of Jiangcheng blocking roads at Hutou — so that gentlemen and ladies of the capital closed their doors early and opened them late.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital you harbored fugitives, blocked the Jiangcheng highway and the lake roads, until men and women of the city dared not venture out until full day.

sentences.zh: 又奪人妻妾，略人子女，徐敖非直失其配匹，乃橫屍道路；

translations.literal: Moreover you seized others' wives and concubines and abducted people's sons and daughters; Xu Ao not only lost his spouse but even had a corpse left on the road;
translations.idiomatic: You seized wives and ravished daughters. Xu Ao did not merely lose his wife — a corpse was left in the street;

sentences.zh: 王伯敖列卿之女，誘為妾媵。

translations.literal: Wang Bo'ao's daughter of a ranked minister you lured to be your concubine.
translations.idiomatic: you abducted Wang Bo'ao's daughter, a minister's child, and kept her as your concubine.

sentences.zh: 我每加掩抑，冀汝自新，了無悛革，怨讎逾甚。

translations.literal: Each time I covered it up and restrained you, hoping you would reform yourself — utterly no repentance; enmity grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again I shielded you and hoped for reform, yet you never repented, and the hatred you earned only grew.

sentences.zh: 遂匹馬奔亡，志懷反噬。

translations.literal: Then on a single horse you fled; your heart harbored intent to bite back.
translations.idiomatic: Then you rode off alone, your heart set on treason.

sentences.zh: 遣信慰問，冀汝能還，果能來歸，遂我夙志。

translations.literal: I sent letters of consolation, hoping you could return; when you truly came back, it fulfilled my long-cherished wish.
translations.idiomatic: I sent messengers urging you to return, and when you did, my old wish was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 謂汝不好文史，志在武功，令汝杖節，董戎前驅。

translations.literal: I said you did not care for letters and learning but set your will on martial achievement; I ordered you to bear the staff and oversee the army as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking you cared little for books but longed for glory in arms, I gave you a commander's staff and made you lead the van.

sentences.zh: 豈謂汝狼心不改，包藏禍胎，志欲覆敗國計，以快汝心。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that your wolf heart would not change, that you would harbor treacherous seed in your womb, your will bent on overturning the state's plan to please your heart!
translations.idiomatic: Who could have known your wolf's heart would never change — that you nursed treason and aimed to ruin the realm for your own satisfaction?

sentences.zh: 今當宥汝以遠，無令房累自隨。

translations.literal: Now I shall pardon you with banishment to a distant place; do not let your household dependents accompany you.
translations.idiomatic: Now I exile you to a distant commandery. Let none of your household go with you.

sentences.zh: 敕所在給汝稟餼。

translations.literal: Order the locality to provide you rations.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities there are to supply your provisions.

sentences.zh: 王新婦、見理等當停太尉間，汝余房累悉許同行。」

translations.literal: Lady Wang the new bride, Jianli, and the rest are to remain quartered in the Grand Marshal's chambers; your other dependents are all permitted to travel together."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang your new wife, Jianli, and certain others will remain in the Grand Marshal's quarters. The rest of your dependents may go with you.

sentences.zh: 於是免官削爵土，徙臨海郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon his office was removed and his nobility and lands cut away; he was banished to Linhai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was stripped of rank and fief and banished to Linhai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 未至徙所，道追赦之。

translations.literal: Before he reached the place of banishment, an edict on the road pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his place of exile, an edict overtook him and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 八年，復封爵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his fief was again restored.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 正德北還，求交朱異。

translations.literal: Zhengde, having returned from the north, sought to become intimate with Zhu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the north, Zhengde sought Zhu Yi's patronage.

sentences.zh: 帝既封昭明諸子，異言正德失職。

translations.literal: The emperor having enfeoffed the sons of Zhaoming, Yi said Zhengde had lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor enfeoffed Zhaoming's sons, Zhu Yi remarked that Zhengde had been left without station.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，特封臨賀郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong he was specially enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong year four he was specially raised to Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 後為丹陽尹，坐所部多劫盜，復為有司所奏，去職。

translations.literal: Later as Governor of Danyang he sat in a district where robbery was rife; again the responsible officials memorialized and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Danyang he presided over a district overrun by bandits. The authorities reported him again and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 出為南兗州，在任苛刻，人不堪命。

translations.literal: He went out to Southern Yan Province; in office he was harsh and cruel, and the people could not bear their lot.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out to govern Southern Yan, he ruled with such cruelty that the people could not endure life.

sentences.zh: 廣陵沃壤，遂為之荒，至人相食噉。

translations.literal: The fertile soil of Guangling was thereby turned to waste, until men even ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: The rich lands of Guangling were laid waste, until men devoured one another.

sentences.zh: 既累試無能，從是黜廢，轉增憤恨，乃陰養死士，常思國釁。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly been tried and found incapable, from this he was demoted and discarded; his resentment grew, and he secretly nurtured death-dedicated men, ever pondering disruption of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly judged unfit for office, he was cast aside, and his hatred deepened. He secretly kept a corps of daredevils and watched for any chance to strike at the state.

sentences.zh: 聚蓄米粟，宅內五十間室，並以為倉。

translations.literal: He hoarded rice and grain; within his residence fifty rooms all were made storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled grain, turning fifty rooms in his mansion into granaries.

sentences.zh: 自征虜亭至於方山，悉略為墅。

translations.literal: From Zhenglu Pavilion to Mount Fangshan he entirely seized as villa estates.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenglu Pavilion to Mount Fangshan he seized every plot for his private estates.

sentences.zh: 蓄奴僮數百，皆黥其面。

translations.literal: He kept several hundred slave retainers, all with their faces tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: He maintained hundreds of slaves, every face tattooed.

sentences.zh: 正德乃以長子見理為太子，以女妻景。

translations.literal: Zhengde then made his eldest son Jianli crown prince and gave his daughter in marriage to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde named his eldest son Jianli crown prince and gave a daughter to Hou Jing in marriage.

sentences.zh: 景為丞相，與約曰：「平城之日，不得全二宮。」

translations.literal: Jing, as Chancellor, agreed with him, saying: "On the day Pingcheng falls, the two palaces shall not be spared intact."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, as chancellor, bargained with him: "When Pingcheng falls, neither palace shall be left whole.

sentences.zh: 又令畿內王侯三日不出者，誅之。

translations.literal: He also ordered that any king or marquis within the capital who did not emerge within three days should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He also decreed that any prince or marquis within the capital who did not show himself within three days was to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 及台城開，正德率眾揮刀欲入，賊先使其徒守門，故正德不果。

translations.literal: When Taicheng opened, Zhengde led his crowd with drawn swords wishing to enter; the rebels first had his followers guard the gates, so Zhengde did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taicheng Gate was breached, Zhengde led his men in with swords drawn, but the rebels had already posted his own followers at the gates, and he could not enter.

sentences.zh: 乃復太清之號，降正德為侍中、大司馬。

translations.literal: Then they restored the reign title Taiqing and demoted Zhengde to Attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels restored the era name Taiqing and demoted Zhengde to Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 正德入問訊，拜且泣。

translations.literal: Zhengde entered to pay respects; he bowed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde came in to pay his respects, bowing and weeping.

sentences.zh: 武帝曰：「惙其泣矣，何嗟及矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "Deep is this weeping — what is there left to sigh for?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said, "Your grief comes too late — what is there now to lament?

sentences.zh: 正德知為賊所賣，深自咎悔，密書與鄱陽嗣王契，以兵入。

translations.literal: Zhengde knew he had been sold by the rebels; deeply he blamed himself. Secretly he wrote to the Prince of Poyang, heir Qi, to bring troops in.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde realized the rebels had used him. He writhed in remorse and secretly wrote the Prince of Poyang, heir Qi, urging him to march in with troops.

sentences.zh: 賊遮得書，乃矯詔殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels intercepted the letter and on a forged edict killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels intercepted the letter and, on forged orders, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 先是，正德妹長樂主適陳郡謝禧，正德奸之，燒主第，縛一婢，加玉釧於手，以金寶附身，聲雲主被燒死，檢取婢屍並金玉葬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhengde's younger sister the Princess of Changle was married to Xie Xi of Chen Commandery; Zhengde debauched her, burned the princess's residence, bound a maidservant, put jade bracelets on her hand, attached gold and gems to her body, proclaimed that the princess had been burned to death, and collected the maid's corpse together with the gold and jade to bury it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhengde's sister the Princess of Changle had married Xie Xi of Chen. Zhengde seduced her, burned down the princess's mansion, bound a servant girl, clasped jade bracelets on her wrists and heaped gold and jewels on her body, then announced that the princess had perished in the fire. He buried the maid's corpse with the jewels, passing it off as the princess's.

sentences.zh: 仍與主通，呼為柳夫人，生二子焉。

translations.literal: Still he carried on with the princess, calling her Lady Liu, and she bore two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He continued the affair with the princess, calling her "Lady Liu," and she bore him two sons.

sentences.zh: 日月稍久，風聲漸露。

translations.literal: As days and months gradually passed, the wind of rumor slowly leaked out.
translations.idiomatic: In time the story began to leak.

sentences.zh: 後黃門郎張准有一雉媒，正德見而奪之。

translations.literal: Later Gentleman at the Yellow Gate Zhang Zhun had a hen pheasant decoy; Zhengde saw it and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Zhun, a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, owned a trained hen pheasant used as a hunting decoy. Zhengde saw it and took it by force.

sentences.zh: 尋會重雲殿為淨供，皇儲以下莫不畢集。

translations.literal: Before long there was a pure offering at the Chongyun Hall; from the crown prince down, none failed to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a Buddhist assembly was held at the Chongyun Hall, and everyone from the crown prince downward attended.

sentences.zh: 准於眾中吒罵曰：「張准雉媒非長樂主，何可略奪！」

translations.literal: Zhun in the crowd shouted and cursed, saying: "Zhang Zhun's pheasant decoy is not the Princess of Changle's — how can it be seized!"
translations.idiomatic: In the crowd Zhang Zhun shouted abuse: "Zhang Zhun's pheasant is not the Princess of Changle's property — who gave you leave to seize it!

sentences.zh: 皇太子恐帝聞之，令武陵王和止之乃休，及出，送雉媒還之。

translations.literal: The crown prince feared the emperor might hear; he had the Prince of Wuling He restrain him and only then stop. On going out he returned the pheasant decoy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince, fearing the emperor would hear, had Prince He of Wuling silence him. After the assembly Zhengde returned the bird.

sentences.zh: 其後梁室傾覆既由正德，百姓至聞臨賀郡名亦不欲道。

translations.literal: Afterward the Liang house's overturning was owing to Zhengde; the common people even, on hearing the name of the Prince of Linhe, did not wish to speak it.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, many blamed Zhengde. People could not bear even to speak the name of the Prince of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 童謠云：「寧逢五虎入市，不欲見臨賀父子。」

translations.literal: A children's song said: "Better to meet five tigers entering the market than to see the father and son of Linhe."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme ran: "Better meet five tigers in the market than lay eyes on the Linhe father and son.

sentences.zh: 其惡之如是。

translations.literal: Such was the hatred of him.
translations.idiomatic: So deeply were they loathed.

sentences.zh: 見理字孟節，性甚凶粗，長劍短衣，出入廛裏，不為宗室所齒。

translations.literal: Jianli, courtesy name Mengjie, by nature was very fierce and coarse; long sword and short coat — he went in and out of market wards and was not deemed fit company by the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli (Mengjie) was brutish by nature, clad in short jacket and long sword, prowling the market alleys. The clan would not acknowledge him.

sentences.zh: 及肆逆，甚得志焉。

translations.literal: When he carried out treason he was very well pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out he was in his element.

sentences.zh: 招聚群盜，每夜輒掠劫，於大航為流矢所中死。

translations.literal: He gathered bands of robbers; every night he plundered; on the Great Ferry he was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered robber bands and raided every night until a stray arrow killed him at the Great Ferry.

sentences.zh: 正德弟正則。

translations.literal: Zhengde's younger brother Zhengze.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde's younger brother was Zhengze.

sentences.zh: 正則字公衡，天監初，以王子封樂山侯。

translations.literal: Zhengze, courtesy name Gongheng, at the beginning of Tianjian as a king's son was enfeoffed as Marquis of Leshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengze (Gongheng) was enfeoffed as Marquis of Leshan at the start of Tianjian, being a king's son.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子洗馬、舍人。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 恒于第內私械百姓令養馬，又盜鑄錢。

translations.literal: He constantly within his residence privately impressed common people to raise horses for him, and again counterfeited coin.
translations.idiomatic: He kept commoners in his mansion by force to rear horses for him and counterfeited coin.

sentences.zh: 大通二年，坐匿劫盜，削爵徙郁林。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong, on account of harboring robbers his nobility was cut and he was banished to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year two he was caught sheltering bandits, stripped of his title, and exiled to Yulin.

sentences.zh: 帝敕廣州日給酒肉，南中官司猶處以侯禮。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Guangzhou to supply him wine and meat daily; the officials of the south still treated him with the ceremonies due a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Guangzhou to provide daily wine and meat, and the southern officials still received him with marquis's honors.

sentences.zh: 正則滋怨諸父，與西江督護靳山顧通室，招誘亡命，將襲番禺。

translations.literal: Zhengze nursed resentment against his uncles; with Gu Tong, military protector of the Western River at Jingshan, he shared his wife, enticed fugitives, and was about to strike Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengze brooded on grievances against his uncles. He took up with Gu Tong, protector of the Western River at Jingshan, sharing the man's wife, and recruited outlaws for a strike on Panyu.

sentences.zh: 未及期而事發，遂鳴鼓會將攻州城。

translations.literal: Before the appointed time the affair leaked; then beating drums he gathered his generals to attack the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointed day the plot was discovered. He beat the drum, mustered his commanders, and attacked the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 刺史元景仲命長史元孝深討之。

translations.literal: The Inspector Yuan Jingzhong ordered the Chief Clerk Yuan Xiaoshen to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yuan Jingzhong sent Chief Clerk Yuan Xiaoshen against him.

sentences.zh: 正則敗，逃於廁，村人縛送之，詔斬於南海。

translations.literal: Zhengze was defeated, fled into a privy, and villagers bound and sent him off; an edict ordered his execution at Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengze was defeated, hid in a latrine, and was seized and bound by villagers. An edict ordered him beheaded at Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 有司請絕屬籍，收妻子。

translations.literal: The responsible officials requested that his name be struck from the clan register and his wife and children seized.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities asked that his line be expunged from the clan register and his wife and children taken.

sentences.zh: 詔聽絕屬籍，妻子特原。

translations.literal: An edict approved striking his name from the clan register; his wife and children were specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved expunging his name but specially spared his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 正則弟正立。

translations.literal: Zhengze's younger brother Zhengli.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengze's younger brother was Zhengli.

sentences.zh: 正立字公山，初封羅平侯。

translations.literal: Zhengli, courtesy name Gongshan, at first was enfeoffed as Marquis of Luoping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengli (Gongshan) was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Luoping.

sentences.zh: 母江有寵。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Jiang enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Jiang, was a favorite.

sentences.zh: 初，正仁之亡，宏溺情曲制，以正立為世子。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Zhengren's death, Hong had indulged feeling and bent the rules, making Zhengli heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengren died, Hong had indulged affection and bent the rules, naming Zhengli heir.

sentences.zh: 正立微有學，宏薨後，知非朝議，表求讓兄，帝甚嘉焉。

translations.literal: Zhengli had a slight measure of learning; after Hong's death, knowing it was not the court's deliberation, he submitted a petition begging to yield to his elder brother; the emperor greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengli had some learning. After Hong's death, knowing the court had not chosen him, he petitioned to yield to his elder brother, which the emperor greatly praised.

sentences.zh: 諸侯例封五百戶，正立改封實土建安縣侯，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: The precedent for princes was an enfeoffment of five hundred households; Zhengli was changed to enfeoffment with substantive territory as Marquis of Jian'an, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were usually granted five hundred households; Zhengli was re-enfeoffed with a substantive fief as Marquis of Jian'an, with a domain of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後位丹陽尹，薨，諡曰敏。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Governor of Danyang; he died, and his posthumous name was Keen.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Danyang, then died; his posthumous name was Keen.

sentences.zh: 子賁嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ben inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ben succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 賁字世文，性躁薄。

translations.literal: Ben, styled Shiwen, was by nature rash and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Ben, styled Shiwen, was rash and shallow by nature.

sentences.zh: 正德為侯景所立，賁出投之，專監造攻具，以攻台城，常為賊耳目。

translations.literal: When Zhengde was installed by Hou Jing, Ben went out to join him, supervised the making of siege engines to attack the Terrace City, and often served as the rebels' eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing installed Zhengde, Ben went over to him, oversaw the building of siege engines against the Terrace City, and often acted as the rebels' spy.

sentences.zh: 南康嗣王會理謀襲景，賁與中宿世子子邕告之，賊矯封賁竟陵王，子邕隨郡王，並改姓侯氏。

translations.literal: Prince Huili, heir of Nankang, plotted to strike Jing; Ben and the heir of Zhongsu, Ziyong, informed on them; the rebels falsely enfeoffed Ben as King of Jingling and Ziyong as King of Su commandery, and both took the surname Hou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huili of Nankang plotted against Jing, Ben and Ziyong, heir of Zhongsu, betrayed the plot; the rebels made Ben king of Jingling and Ziyong king of Su commandery and gave them the surname Hou.

sentences.zh: 賁為宗正卿，子邕都官尚書，專權陵蔑朝政，居嘗晝臥，見柳敬禮、蕭勸入室驅之，賁驚起乞恩。

translations.literal: Ben became Minister of the Imperial Clan and Ziyong Minister of the Court of Justice; they monopolized power and looked down on court affairs. Once Ben was napping by day when he saw Liu Jingli and Xiao Quan enter the room to drive him out; Ben started up in alarm and begged for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Ben became minister of the imperial clan and Ziyong minister of justice; they dominated the court with contempt. Once Ben napped by day; Liu Jingli and Xiao Quan entered and drove him out, and Ben leapt up begging for mercy.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊惡其翻覆，殺之。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels hated his fickleness and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels, hating his treachery, killed him.

sentences.zh: 正立弟正表，封封山侯，後奔樂山。

translations.literal: Zhengli's younger brother Zhengbiao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengshan and later fled to Leshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengli's younger brother Zhengbiao was made marquis of Fengshan and later fled to Leshan.

sentences.zh: 正表弟正信。

translations.literal: Zhengli's younger cousin was Zhengxin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengli's younger cousin was Zhengxin.

sentences.zh: 正信字公理，封武化侯。

translations.literal: Zhengxin, styled Gongli, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuhua.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxin, styled Gongli, was enfeoffed as marquis of Wuhua.

sentences.zh: 與正立同生，亦被宏鍾愛。

translations.literal: Born to the same mother as Zhengli, he was also cherished by Hong.
translations.idiomatic: A uterine brother of Zhengli, he was also cherished by Hong.

sentences.zh: 然幼不慧，常執白團扇，湘東王取題八字銘玩之。

translations.literal: Yet in youth he was not clever; he always carried a white round fan. The Prince of Xiangdong took it and inscribed an eight-character motto to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: But he was dull as a boy and always carried a white round fan; Prince Yi of Xiangdong inscribed an eight-character motto on it to mock him.

sentences.zh: 正信不知嗤之，終常搖握。

translations.literal: Zhengxin did not know he was being ridiculed and to the end often waved and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxin never understood the mockery and to the end kept waving it about.

sentences.zh: 位給事中，卒。

translations.literal: He held the post of Attendant Within the Gates and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant within the gates and died.
